I have 35 hours in Resident Evil 9 Requiem and I also have every achievement (100%). This is, in my opinion, one of the best, maybe the best modern RE game. After 4 playthroughs, I still didn’t feel bored because the game is just so fun. The graphics are extremely good and one of the best in modern games.  The gameplay is just peak, both as Leon and as Grace. If you didn’t know, in Resident Evil 9 Requiem you are playing as 2 different characters: Leon S. Kennedy (appears in RE2, RE4, RE6 and RE9) and Grace Ashcroft (a new character in the series, daughter of Alice Ashcroft). It is not like RE2, in which you can play 2 campaigns as either Leon or Claire. In RE9 you play one campaign with both characters. So you play a bit with Grace, then with Leon, then with Grace again, and so on.  Leon’s sections/gameplay are focused on action and fast gameplay. You will kill many zombies with hand cannons, shotguns, snipers, and of course the new weapon in RE9, the Requiem. A really big Magnum that does a lot of damage. Both Grace and Leon will use this weapon, but at the start at least, ammo is very limited for it.  As Leon, you will also have your hatchet, a combat axe instead of a knife like in RE2 and RE4, for example. Leon is 49 years old in RE9 and really badass. Nice new black jacket, wristwatch, and a new car, a Porsche. Some enemies will also drop their big melee weapons when they die. Leon can then pick them up and throw or swing them at the nearest enemy. This is really cool and increases the cinematic and action-heavy feeling when playing Leon.  His one-liners are great, not the best in the series, but they don’t disappoint. There is no merchant, but there is a “storage box” from which you can buy new guns, upgrade them, sell guns, and buy armor, ammo, and healing items with credits. You get credits from killing enemies or finding them as items.  In the first half of the game, Leon’s sections are really short, but towards the mid and late game, Leon will appear a lot more often. So the first half of the game is more focused on Grace and the second one more on Leon, but both appear in both “halves”.  Grace’s gameplay is not action-heavy, but really scary. While Leon plays like action horror, Grace plays like normal survival horror. Very, very limited ammo at the start, multiple stalkers and big enemies throughout her sections, and a great crafting system.  In RE9 there aren’t many puzzles, and if they are there, they are not very hard or good, so that’s kinda sad. But the general gameplay, gameplay ideas, and a few sections as Grace are just extremely great, really, really great.  So Grace’s sections are a lot harder than Leon’s sections, more scary and more strategic and tense. It’s peak.  The story is pretty good as well. It is kinda a follow-up to RE2 because it also takes place in Raccoon City for a big part of the game and also in the RPD police station, and the T-Virus is back in the game. And RE9 also gives you a lot of lore for older titles, which is very nice.  The game runs very, very well. Someone could even run it easily on a 1050 while still looking good. Great optimization.  The replayability comes from the extra mode “Leon Must Die Forever” and obviously the cool challenges. There are many, and if you ever wanted to 100% a RE game, do this one. It is the easiest to 100%. It takes 3 playthroughs and is not that hard.  If you complete a challenge, you get challenge points that you can then spend on special items like bonus weapons, infinite knives/hatchets, infinite ammo, or a rocket launcher (infinite as well), or concept art or models.  After completing the game, you will also get a kind of making-of video and “Grace’s Report” that explains the Raccoon City incident in detail for you. You can also purchase a map of the collectibles in the game, the Mr. Raccoon figures, in black and white, so finding them is very easy.  The game has 4 difficulty options: Casual, Standard (Modern), Standard (Classic), and Insanity. Insanity only unlocks after completing the game at least once on any difficulty.  Casual is just the easiest. Standard (Modern) is like current modern games, and Standard (Classic) is a bit harder and you will need ink ribbons to save, just like in the older titles.  All difficulties are fun and have their use in getting 100%.  If you want to 100% the game in 3 runs, do it like this: First run: Standard (Classic), get all collectibles, files, open all safes/containers, get the miscellaneous achievements, and complete the game. Second run: Casual mode, finish the game in under 4 hours, without healing, and don’t use the Blood Collector as Grace. That is a crafting item which allows Grace to collect blood and craft things with it like ammo and other items. Third run: Complete the game on Insanity difficulty.  I recommend Extriaa on YouTube. He makes really good guides on those runs and he will help you a lot, trust me.  Generally, the game is a masterpiece and you will love it if you are a Resident Evil fan, classic or modern. Especially if you loved RE2. The game takes about 8–10 hours to finish (took me 7:41 on my first playthrough), but it is not hard to do it in under 4 hours if you do it right.  Hope this review helped you out. Can’t say much about Leon Must Die Forever mode because I never played it. It is not supposed to be very good.  But the base game is, and DLC coming soon so be excited.  Bye

The game feels like RE2R and 4R did a fusion dance and this is the result. It feels like two very different games depending on which section you are on.  The Grace sections felt like RE2R. Wander around, find key items, decide how best to spend your limited resources, solve puzzles. The classic RE experience. There were really no changes of note from how RE2R plays worth mentioning. There are some changes that I won't spoil, but nothing groundbreaking. I did play Grace's 1st section in 1st person, and it felt very similar to RE7. I imagine this would carry on into the rest of the game, but I can't say since I switched to 3rd person after the intro as I much prefer 2R and 4R to 7 and 8. If you like 2R or 7 you will like her sections.  The Leon sections felt like RE4R on steroids. The changes and evolutions they made to the combat were so sick. I just wish there were more chainsaw sections. Again, just like the Grace sections, none of the changes were huge, but for whatever reason I enjoyed them far more than the changes for Grace's gameplay. I tried 1st person for about 5 minutes before going back to 3rd. It was fine, but it just didn't feel nearly as good to me.  The story was pretty good. Nothing incredible, but it leaves you looking forward to what they do next.  Now for the issues I have with the game.  It's short. I finished it blind in 9.5 hours. This is longer than my first 2R playthrough, but remember this is split into what is basically 2 different games. I spent over 30 finishing all 4 scenarios in 2R. And I think my first playthrough of 4R took around 25. I know you are supposed to replay these games, but without the scenarios of 2R or the expansiveness of 4R, I just had no desire to do it again. Maybe I'll go back and do Insanity at some point, but I just didn't have the urge to start over again immediately like I did for 2R or 4R. Hell I even replayed 3R immediately despite it's short comings.  Additionally, the split of the two very distinct paths combined with the brevity leaves the game feeling underdeveloped. The satisfaction of growing power you get from 4R is largely absent as you don't get a wide enough variety of weapons or enough playtime to get the same enjoyment from the long, slow build up of power from upgrades with Leon.  The gratification of deciphering the intricate web of items, puzzles and how to spend your resources required to progress from 2R is absent as the Grace sections aren't long enough to have enough items or enemies to make your decisions and puzzle solving very satisfying. Both paths end up feeling like shadows of their incredible predecessors despite the changes and upgrades made to them.  Overall a pretty good game, but the short playtime and split paths left me feeling I didn't get my money's worth. I again wish Steam had a neutral option, because if I had waited a year or two to get it and the game was $30 I would whole heartedly recommend it. I just can't advise you to get it at the current price point.

[h1]THE END OF THE BEGINNING[/h1]  My long journey of experiencing every possible [b]Resident Evil[/b] title has finally come to an end. What started as a simple idea a month or two ago turned into a full series marathon, taking me through the highs, lows, remakes, classics, and everything in between. And at last, that journey brought me to [b]Resident Evil Requiem[/b].  First of all, the game looks absolutely incredible. This is hands down the best-looking Resident Evil title to date. The environments, lighting, character models, and overall presentation are stunning. That being said, there is one technical issue that stood out to me. When using ray or path tracing, and especially ray reconstruction, the visual artifacts and noticeable "boiling" effect can be quite distracting at times. It's something I hope Capcom continues to improve because the game's visuals deserve to shine without those issues.  As for the gameplay, I think Capcom did a fantastic job blending different eras of [b]Resident Evil[/b] together. Leon's side of the story feels like a natural evolution of the more action-oriented entries, while Grace's sections borrow heavily from the horror-focused approach of [b]Resident Evil 7[/b] and [b]Resident Evil Village[/b]. The result is a great balance between action, tension, exploration, and survival horror that manages to appeal to fans of both styles.  The atmosphere is excellent throughout the entire game. There were plenty of moments where I felt that familiar tension creeping in, always expecting something to be lurking around the next corner. At the same time, the game never forgets its roots and constantly reminds you why this franchise has remained so iconic for nearly three decades.  Story-wise, I really enjoyed the plot twists and the way the narrative circles back to the very foundations of the series. Learning more about [b]Oswell E. Spencer[/b], Umbrella's origins, and the events that shaped the [b]Resident Evil[/b] universe made the story feel like a love letter to longtime fans. After spending weeks playing through the entire franchise, seeing everything connect back to where it all began felt incredibly rewarding.  More than anything, [b]Resident Evil Requiem[/b] felt like revisiting old memories. It reminded me why I started this journey in the first place. The game is packed with details, references, and connections that longtime fans will appreciate, while also planting seeds for the future of the franchise.  Personally, I have a feeling that the mysterious organization - [b]The Connections[/b] will continue to play a major role moving forward. They've spent so much time operating from the shadows that it feels like their story is only beginning.  Before we get there, though, let's hope Capcom has an amazing DLC planned for this game because I'm definitely not ready to leave this world behind just yet.  After all these games, all these viruses, all these conspiracies, and all these years of [b]Resident Evil[/b] history, [b]Requiem[/b] feels like both an ending and the beginning of something new - and that's exactly what a great finale should feel like!

Soy fan de la saga desde el primer Resident Evil de 1996, y este juego te deja un sabor de boca buenísimo, y te das cuenta de que esta saga está en su segunda edad dorada, y esperemos que siga así por mucho tiempo.

What If You Combined The Resident Evil 4 Formula And The Resident Evil 7 Survival Horror At Its Best , And Then Spiced It With Nostalgia? You Would Get Resident Evil 9 (Requiem).   Don't Forget About Its Outstanding Visual - The Graphics Are Absolute Fire And The Art Style Is Just Awesome. Its Enemies , Especially At The Hospital , Are Damn Interesting And Unique (Some Are Repetitive , Sadly) With Their Own Behaviour Patterns. The Hospital Is My Personal Favourite. Its Aesthetics And Enemies Make It Simply Unforgettable. And The Horror Element In This Game Is Literally Next Level.  The Choice To Make Two Protagonists With Their Own Gameplay Was Just Perfect. You're Sweating Your Ass Off While Running Away And Hiding From The Enemies As Grace , Feeling Her Pain And Fear In Each Cutscene And With Each Movement She Makes. She's An Unexperienced , Fragile Young Lady , And Her Gameplay Perfectly Suits Her. And Then There's Leon - The Favourite Character Of Many RE Fans - A DSO Operative With Years Of Combat Experience. His Gameplay Is Quick-Paced And Intense , Just Like In RE4 , With Leon Hunting His Enemies , And Not The Other Way Around. The Game Switches Between Them , Giving The Player An Emotional Roller Coaster.  Emotions. This Game , Resident Evil Requiem , May Or May Not Be The Best Resident Evil Game , But To Me - It's Easily A Masterpiece And My New Favourite. Because This Game Is About Emotions You Recieve From It. And Games , In The First Place , Are Made To Bring You Those Priceless , Unforgettable Emotions. Fear , Joy , Awe , Sadness - Resident Evil Requiem Evokes Those And Masterfully Combines Them , Making Sure You're Never Bored And Constantly Involved In The Story.  Thank You , Capcom , For Resident Evil Requiem. Thank You For The Entire RE Series.  10/10.

This is an excellent addition to the series, and a worthy Resident Evil game. It combines the recent successes of the series' foray into first person survival horror (RE 7/8) with the third person action-survival-horror of the remake trilogy (RE 2/3/4 Remakes). The playable character and tone of the game alternate between slower-paced tension with Grace, and the faster, more action oriented gameplay of Leon, a series regular. For most of the game, this flows well from one character's perspective to the next, but it does create a few pacing issues in certain parts. There are a few more questionable design choices, but overall this is a great game in it's own right, and a fantastic Resident Evil story.   Frankly, if you care at all about the storyline of these games, Requiem is a must-play.

I'm about as old school RE as they come, only begrudgingly accepting the action direction the series has flirted with over the years. Requiem is essentially 2 resident evil games packaged together, and I feel like it will satisfy both types of fans. For me, Grace is a fun protagonist who I appreciate being genuinely scared of the monsters she encounters. Her sections are pure survival horror and its some of the best the series has to offer with fun puzzles, interesting ways to navigate through enemies, and good resource management. Leon contrast this by being a grizzled veteran who was over zombies 10 years ago. His sections are quick action set-pieces using a revised version of how he controls in RE4 remake. Its a great reward after going through some horror just to relieve some stress as Leon for 20 minutes. The only real problems I have with the game is how bad the story gets after the half-way point. I haven't cared for the direction RE lore has taken since RE4 and I don't think the big reveals of this story are interesting. My problems are mainly lore related though, and the silly action set-piece or character exchanges don't really bother me. It isn't offensive, I just wish they took a different direction. Either way its worth it, even at full price.

There will be no spoilers in this review. I want people to know what they’re walking into without having the experience taken away.   [h1]Let’s Clear the Air…[/h1]  Yes, it’s nostalgia bait. Yes, it lacks innovative gameplay and narrative. Yes, it’s pretty damn awesome.  These are the most important things one should know prior to playing ‘Resident Evil: Requiem.’ This is a game that doesn’t push boundaries yet understands what makes this series work. If you enjoyed the last ten years of ‘Resident Evil’ I have no doubt in my mind, you’ll pick this up with ease. If you read that and believe you’re looking for more, that’s fine! From what I’ve gathered, the reception is split between a majority who love it and those who wanted something new to bite into. If you agree with the ladder, you’ll walk out disappointed. Even then, it’s worthwhile to see what’s in store. It’s hard to envision someone not loving Requiem when you see Leon paint a room red, or watching Grace nearly lose her mind as you evade unimaginable horrors.  [h1]The Nitty, With a Lotta Gritty[/h1]  The setup is simple. Grace Ashcroft, a competent but inexperienced FBI agent finds herself in a living nightmare. As Grace faces the inconceivable, Leon Kennedy is hot on her trail. A seasoned veteran, Leon is rarely frightened and too tired to deal with anything’s BS. These dynamics play off each other well. Grace is an incredible character, with a heart wrenching story that fuels her search for answers; Leon’s fed up and ready to kick in any door. They’re my favorite characters in the series, easily.   This set-up is as good as it gets. The most essential element of a survival horror game is motivation. The ‘Silent Hill’ games understand this perfectly, but RE has always been close behind.  Even when I’m controlling a character that lacks the resources to conquer a situation, I still wanna go on. I identify with Grace. Her desire is to find meaning in the horrific things she’s endured; she wants purpose in the suffering. With how vividly they paint her past, you want to push on.   Leon is different. The guy is a powerhouse. Even in old age, he’s constantly moving. He loads ♥♥♥♥ up and tears it down like we’ve never seen before. His skill and instinct are something I admire, and pity. He’s a killing machine but what he could have been was a beat cop. Leon is just as damaged as Grace; he wants atonement for the past he could have had.  For what the game is, this dichotomy between Grave and Leon’s gameplay feels reflective of my experience with these games.  [h1]Kennedy and Ashcroft, Just Like Me[/h1]  I’ve had an on-off relationship with the franchise. I played RE7 a decade ago, then RE2R a few years later. I loved them but never found myself tackling the series. One of my good friends, Joey, gave me RE1R. He’s a huge fan of the games, so I felt something of a responsibility to sit down and play it.  Within the span of a month, I steamrolled the games. They were dropping like mutated bees. Every game, I grew closer to the characters and the work that went into making them. RE9 was fast approaching and my excitement couldn’t be quelled.  Somewhere along the line, a new feeling appeared. A longing that I couldn’t explain.   The world of ‘Resident Evil’ and the experiences in them, it makes me mad. It’s horrifying, upsetting, saddening. I feel for these characters and the people they couldn’t save. ‘Umbrella’ will be a company I think of when the price of insulin goes up another $300.   We’re losing our hope to those in power, in search of one thing: that profit. What good is our well-being when there’s thousands of dollars made on single doses of medication? Why is our autonomy important when these people obviously know what’s best for us? These are some ways organized bodies dehumanize us. We must fight so groups like ‘Umbrella’ and ‘The Connections’ can’t exist.   We’ve gotta be Grace and Leon. We must search for answers; we must press the line. We need to be afraid, and we need to kick some heads in. Otherwise, what little ability we had will be taken away if it hasn’t already.   [h1]In Conclusion…[/h1] Check it out, or don’t, it’s your money!

Resident Evil Requiem is a fantastic game. The two protagonists offer completely different playstyles. Grace is trying to survive. Leon is treating the zombie apocalypse like another Tuesday.  I am still not entirely sure whether I would have preferred two separate campaigns. Part of me wanted more time with both characters.  The graphics are fantastic and the game runs surprisingly well. Everything feels polished and finished, which sadly is not something I take for granted anymore.  The game weaponizes nostalgia against anyone who has been playing Resident Evil for a long time. Going back to parts of Raccoon City and seeing places that I first experienced in the late 90s and early 2000s hit surprisingly hard. The developers knew exactly what they were doing and my memberberries never stood a chance.  The story was much richer than I expected. It answers a few questions and ties up some loose ends, but somehow manages to create even more questions in the process. Whether that is a good thing probably depends on how deep someone is into Resident Evil lore. I am definitely not the right person to judge that, because keeping up with the full story of this series feels like it requires about ten hours of YouTube videos and a conspiracy board on the wall.  The orphanage is back. It was not quite as painful as in the RE2 Remake, but the whole hide-and-cover routine was still annoying.  Gunplay feels top notch and fits both characters perfectly. That said, I got scammed quite a few times, especially later in the game. There were many situations where I expected an enemy to be stunned from a shot to the leg, only to find out they were currently in some random animation that apparently made them immune to being stunned. This was especially annoying because stunning enemies is a huge part of both characters' toolkits. For Grace it is often the difference between getting past an enemy or not, and for Leon it means introducing their face to his ridiculously overpowered axe.

Eu nunca tinha jogado nenhum Resident Evil na vida.  Na verdade, só fui parar em Resident Evil porque ganhei o jogo numa promoção da NVIDIA quando comprei uma placa de vídeo nova. Ele ficou parado na minha biblioteca por uns três meses até que um dia eu olhei os gráficos, pensei "isso aqui tá bonito demais pra ficar pegando poeira" e resolvi dar uma chance.  Ainda bem que fiz isso.  Eu não sou fã de jogos de terror. Na real, esse provavelmente foi o primeiro jogo do gênero que eu realmente joguei até o final. E mesmo sem jogar de fone, sem apagar a luz e sem toda aquela imersão de maluco que gosta de tomar susto, o jogo me pegou completamente.  Primeiro porque ele não depende daqueles jumpscares vagabundos e baratos pra te assustar. Existe uma tensão constante, um suspense muito bem construído, principalmente no começo, mas sempre de forma inteligente. A história também é muito mais interessante do que eu esperava e me prendeu do início ao fim.  A gameplay é absurda de boa. Tudo é fluido, responsivo e gostoso de jogar. Leon e Grace são personagens excelentes e, mesmo eu não tendo qualquer ligação emocional com a franquia, a Capcom conseguiu me fazer gostar deles muito rápido.  Mas eu preciso falar dos gráficos.  Os gráficos são simplesmente **absurdos, absurdos, absurdos**. Sem exagero, esse é facilmente um dos 3 jogos mais bonitos que eu já joguei na vida. O nível de detalhe é assustador. As expressões faciais, a iluminação, os cenários e principalmente as partes de gore são tão bem feitas que às vezes chegam a ser desconfortáveis.  Comecei jogando numa RTX 5070 Ti e depois continuei numa RTX 5090. Obviamente hardware ajuda, mas o mérito aqui é da Capcom. A otimização é excelente e, pra quem tiver a oportunidade de jogar com tudo no máximo e Path Tracing ativado, a experiência é absurda.  Teve momento que alguns personagens pareciam mais reais do que eu quando olho no espelho.  E o maior elogio que eu posso fazer é simples: terminei o jogo em cerca de 12 ou 13 horas e imediatamente fui atrás de mais Resident Evil. Comprei Resident Evil 4 Remake logo depois de zerar porque eu simplesmente não queria sair daquela fórmula.  E o melhor é que o jogo não acaba quando os créditos sobem. Assim que terminei, já comecei outra run para fazer desafios. Depois fiz a run de velocidade, terminei em menos de 4 horas e já emendei uma terceira no modo mais difícil, aquele nível de dificuldade reservado para quem claramente tem algum problema psicológico.  Mesmo repetindo a campanha, existe progressão. Você desbloqueia perks, skins, melhorias, desafios e objetivos novos. O jogo te dá motivo para continuar jogando sem parecer uma lista de tarefas infinita.  A Capcom acertou em cheio. O combate é excelente, os personagens funcionam, a campanha tem ritmo, os gráficos são absurdos e a rejogabilidade é muito maior do que eu esperava.  O resultado é que um cara que nunca tinha jogado Resident Evil virou fã da franquia.  E agora eu estou genuinamente animado para jogar os outros jogos e já deixei o próximo Resident Evil na minha lista de desejos.  Se um jogo consegue transformar um completo novato em fã, alguma coisa ele fez muito certo.

All I can say without the cliché of being a diehard fan of the Resident Evil franchise ever since the 4th original game, I've been with this series through all the mainline games that are available on Steam and what I want to say is that Requiem is by far an easy S+ tier game up in the top with the original 4, remake 4 and 7.   When I first seen the trailers I was scared that this game will be some sort of crap-show of trying to combine the two worlds that are right now in the RE Franchise, the first person more focused horror aspects that were introduced with Ethan's games since RE7 and the action-packed gameplay that we're used to with Leon. I am happy that I have been proven wrong, the fact that we have Grace, a new character in this franchise that is experiencing all the Umbrella's horrors first hand makes the horrors aspects to be absolutely wonderful, and Leon...well he never disappoints, roundhouse kicks everywhere, aura farmer, cheesy one-liners, everything that we know and love from him, no more unnecessary backflips, tho...age sure is a curse, isn't it?   So yea, this review is already long, and in order to not make it longer, game's great, I just love it and wanna replay it as soon as possible to make a 100% completion, indeed it seems a little simple or easier, but I think that's just because I am used to the RE formula and what to expect, friends of mine who played this as their 2nd or 3rd RE game ever, felt the complete opposite, but if you want more challenge, just play on the hardest difficulty available from the start, that's what I did and it was fine. There's not much to say negative about the game, other that it feels a little short and it's difficulty is not very high, but these aren't some deal breaks for me. Haven't encountered any major problems or game-breaking bugs, I took a little performance impact at the 3rd-ish area of the game, but that's mostly because of my hardware and that I was streaming at the time, can't blame the game for that since I haven't tested it enough, but other than that, I don't have any major complains that wouldn't make this game a good product. Overall I enjoyed Requiem very much & think it's a great game. But, over the last few years I've been spoiled a bit by excellent survival horror games that stick to the tried & true formula without gimmicks & the kind of playable cutscene QTEs that have been a staple of RE ever since 4. Whether it's been the smaller budgets, or remaking an older game & sticking to its roots, but games like the Silent Hill 2 remake, Dead Space remake, Cronos recently & some indies lacking the resources to script a ton of railroaded bombastic setpieces forcing them to stick to the basic formula of puzzles-metroidvania exploration in labyrinthine environments, managing your resources, inventory as you pick your fights & navigate obstacles-- But I find that those are the perfect blend of ingredients right there to make a really good game that's varied enough, especially if you then also remember to pace yourself with progression, story beats, enemy variety, environmental variety.  Capcom still seems to fear the casual gamer getting bored & needing variety for variety's sake, and so we get forced heavily scripted stealth sections with Grace (it's no Mister X even which at least was a bit more dynamic), we get long intros of walking around lightly interacting or fighting a zombie in a QTE, Leon gets classic minecart-- I mean motorcycle sections where you have limited control, a few scripted sequences with a couple of bosses before you actually get to fight them. All of this is stuff I really don't care for and kind of ruins re/play value.   - The Care center section, specifically from when Leon hands Grace his Requiem up until Grace jumps down into the basement, is a 10/10 experience, the environment is gorgeous, the gameplay finely tuned, enemies have such a good personality to them-- It's classic RE taking a lot of the best elements from the RPD & I assume the classic mansion. But that care center section is maybe 1/5th, or 1/4th if we're generous, of the entire game.  - I actually really enjoyed the Leon Raccoon City section, from when we arrive in our car up until we blow up the gate, I think it's solid, it's not as good as RE4, but it's solid, a 8/10 on RE-scale (& there are dookies). That too is maybe 1/4th of the game though, sandwiched between all the guided sections, setpiece sections, QTE sections and forced stealth sections. Post that it's just lesser RE, labs & stuff.  - The gimmick bonus game mode "Leon must die forever" was actually relatively fun for a while if simple. It's been a while since I've played mercenaries so I don't know how it compares off the top of my head, but it never grabbed me in for instance the RE4/r which I replay the campaign a lot of (even though it too has gimmicks, de lago fight & minecarts, at least on replays Ashley can be put in comedic armor to make her section an easy skip), but mercenaries fans seem to dislike the game mode here. No new game+ only the content shop, but on replays they do at least give Leon early access to his item box from the start and slightly remix some encounters & loot.  The demo gives you an idea of the worst of what the game has to offer in some sense, because it's just the scripted intro where you don't get to play as Grace properly set loose in the Care center. But the demo did do its job for me to buy this since I saw playthroughs & knew I'd love the care center & raccoon city parts which I did want to experience for myself, & I was mainly worried about the performance & how ugly it might look without path tracing given some horrendous influencer promotional hype backed by Nvidia.  Luckily it didn't look bad at all-- Small caveat, I did use the RE9 Graphics Enhancement Mod by JoHien from Nexus, which properly enables contact shadows for everything which Capcom deliberately disabled, whether it's been to falsely advertise Nvidia sponsored tech or they have some other reason, but the mod is well worth it for people who don't even care for RT/PT & want to boost the quality of rasterized rendering beyond its gimped defaults.  I've never put too much stock in the story of RE, it's cheesy & a fever dream, but every actor puts in a good performance here & it is a joy to follow.  I'm hoping whatever future DLC they make isn't going to be gimmick riddled, if we could get another RE4R Separate Ways that would be great, but not a Shadows of Rose. And hopefully Capcom won't listen to CEO & security engineer brainworms about needing more DRM and anti modding measures because that's lame & kills replayability of their games even more. I'm assuming RE9 will follow the trend of removing Denuvo 6-18months post last DLC/content update but they'll still try sneaking Enigma or equivalent into it, hopefully people will slap sense into them once more.  Still, the core gameplay is great, Leon is great, Grace is great, I enjoyed the locations even though I know I'm in a minority who puts the Raccoon City section high, but it's because it's just classic gameplay without taking control away from the player & it's fun to play as Leon. Didn't have bugs, crashes, was disappointed by lack of exclusive fullscreen support which Capcom seems to have ditched since Pragmata too lacked it, but otherwise ran pretty well & looked good though textures & streaming of them is still a problem for Capcom. I would prefer a very polished survival horror experience OR a more fleshed out action-focused campaign, rather than a good but limited survival horror with 5 minutes clunky action breaks for the first half of the game, then having the second half almost entirely happening in the fifty shades of grey city with a main character that moves like he has a broom up his *** and enemies that won't flinch with a point blank shotgun shot.  While those are more subjectives, I also found the upgrade systems interesting but undercooked (coming late for Leon and unbalanced), the new characters not captivating or superfluous, ridiculous moments that would make RE6 blush and "dramatic" events really forced, as they mostly involve characters we basically know nothing about and didn't have time to appreciate. The additional playthroughs also made me realize it's one of the least replayable campaign in the series, since it's really linear and the combat isn't satisfying enough. The game is not too hard, it's not terrible, it tried some interesting things, but it ends up feeling both very ambitious and undercooked.   I would give it a more objective 7.5/10 for the interesting ideas and visual polish, but just judging from the actual fun I had while playing, it would be more like a 6 or 6.5.

While I do think this is a decent game and enjoyed my first playthrough, it has far too many shortcomings.  After multiple playthroughs, the cracks in this game really start to show. For starters, the story is absolutely abysmal, even by Capcom standards. Nothing makes sense here & I doubt this is even a debate. Hopefully the DLC can address some of the plot holes.  Secondly, there is next to zero innovation. This game relies too heavily on fan service, to the point you as a player almost start to feel guilty. Leon is as cheesy as ever and has a few cool new combat mechanics, that's about it. Grace's sections are just generic first person horror sequences that somehow didn't even feel like Resident Evil. Zeno is essentially a goofy Wesker clone who, despite his immense aura, adds nothing meaningful to the story. You also return to the RPD, which is initially exciting and was a major selling point of the title, but on subsequent playthroughs it feels more like a useless obstacle you just walk through to continue the rest of the game. If Capcom is willing to sacrifice good game design just to make tourists happy, the future of this franchise looks bleak.  Thirdly, don't even think about replaying this game more than twice, because it quickly becomes one of the most monotonous gaming experiences ever. It takes nearly half an hour before the actual game begins, and then there's another 15 min repetitive walking sim section halfway through. These are fine on a first playthrough, but they should have been accounted for in ng+.  Speaking of ng+, this game doesn't have it. Instead, it features the most monotonous "hard mode" I've ever seen in an RE game. The insanity difficulty is essentially standard mode, except every enemy now takes a ridiculous amount of bullets to kill. This isn't great game design, instead it's artificial challenge and only serves to be incredibly frustrating.  This really isn't a bad game if you're only planning to play through it once and then put it down. However, 70 euros does not sit right with me.

An incredible game from start to finish. Requiem continues the story of Leon and introduces Grace Ashcroft into the narrative for the first time. It is recommended to have played at least RE 2 before playing this game as this game does take place in Raccoon City again later in the game. This story will feel much better connected if you got to experience the previous game(s) beforehand.  The story itself is very good for a RE game, tying up loose ends along the way and introducing new lore that obviously hints at more future games coming out that continue the canon after this game. With the announcement of the Veronica remake happening officially, will likely expect RE10 or RE: X to come out in a couple years time.  The game play in general is so satisfying. I like the shift between Grace's survival horror to Leon's more action horror. The pacing is kept very smooth all throughout, never getting boring. With Grace, you are more often sneaking to assassinate enemies, while Leon is guns blazing with some assassination opportunities sprinkled in. I chose to play in 3rd person the entire game since I like to see the characters. What is so cool is that in 3rd person, you can visibly see Grace quivering in fear when enemies walk close by and you can see their head tracking where the enemy is as they breath more erratically. When aiming down sights with a gun, you an really see her hand shaking in fear, while Leon's is a lot more steady with confidence. This level of detail is the kind of immersion I crave, and this game delivers that in spades.  Overall, this is one of the best RE games to date. Cannot recommend this game enough for fans of Resident Evil and horror games in general. Definitely GOTY contender if I have ever seen one for those that care about accolades.

SPOILERS!  to preface I've only played RE2, RE3, RE4, RE5, RE7 RE8 and now requiem with a small amount of time with RE6  Resident Evil Requiem is a very conflicting experience. It has some of the best parts of the Resident Evil series yet and some of the worst. It presents itself as a Michelin-star dish, but in the middle it's cold and unappetizing.  Requiem's opening sets the tone, with the Care Center being one of the best-designed mansions/sections in all of Resident Evil, with the atmosphere and layout of the rooms creating tension, along with new interesting and mysterious characters developing throughout Requiem (Grace, Victor Gideon, Emily). At the peak of RE9, we leave the Care Center to be introduced to some rip-off slog of Wesker, and that's where the game jumps off a cliff.  It goes from some of the most intense and thrilling survival horror gameplay in all of Resident Evil to a fan-service slop Leon shooter. I'm convinced Leon was only pitched and added to the game because they knew it'd sell more. Leon comes into this game as the heroic hero and ends no different. You could replace Leon's character with anyone else in the series, and it wouldn't affect this game in the slightest. I like Leon as much as the next guy, but after the first hour of being in Raccoon City, I already felt myself wanting to go back to Grace. Almost all of Raccoon City is nostalgia slop. Mr. X, RPD, spiders, Robert Kendo flashbacks—seriously? None of this serves any purpose to the plotline. Not to mention that Raccoon City feels like some TLOU2-inspired slop.  The actual survival aspect of Requiem isn't as well executed as RE4 Remake. In RE4 Remake, my lack of resources and supplies makes me have a sense of survival, but in Requiem, all of that is thrown out the window. Money is extremely easily obtained, and upgrades don't feel as hard or meaningful to unlock, with always having leftover money to buy ammo since it's insanely cheap. The combat itself is improved in many ways in Requiem, but it also feels like it takes a step back in many ways as well.  Boss fights are easily the worst in the series, with none of them being memorable besides The Commander (HUNK), and it's actually laughable how rip-off Wesker goes out. He's a character that's displayed to have importance in the story, just for the story to never develop his character. In the end, he's pointless with no depth (he might just be a tease of something bigger to come in RE10, but regardless).  It also has the WORST section/level in any Resident Evil: the Orphanage. It's astonishing how badly designed it is, not to mention how painfully boring it is. The entire 10-minute section is sitting under a table for 5 minutes and running for another 5. It's horrible, and don't even get me started on the hallway and how unintuitive it is.  The pacing and story are horrible after the Care Center. They switch between both action and survival horror, and the idea is good, but the execution is done poorly. It could have worked if the game were more than 10 hours long, but instead it feels like two different games mashed into one, which makes it miss many of the emotional beats Requiem should have but doesn't.  Seriously, the entire game basically drives itself off a cliff after the Care Center. It just turns out that Zeno and Victor are both just dumbasses and no mind-controlling superweapon ever existed, and no one dies, not even Emily. Are we serious? It's all just sunshine and rainbows? If we're being honest, Leon should have died in this game, but Capcom doesn't have the balls to kill off their big money maker. They do, however, decide to add a non-canon option to kill him off. It just feels like they wanted to have their cake and eat it too.  Resident Evil has been fun, and this one is no different. It's still a fun game, but it's turning into the same type of fun as Marvel and Disney movies. Requiem looks good, plays good, feels good, with loads of fan service, but the story is lacking and felt to me as the developers scrambling to try to sell the most copies by using the cheapest methods possible, ending up with one of the most shallow Resident Evils to date.  Again, it's a good game. I'm just thoroughly disappointed. Maybe my expectations were too high after all the 9/10s across the board. I did enjoy my time for the most part.  List of things it did good:  -Care Center (which is like half the game, thankfully) -Grace (as a character she is great, but again becomes pretty dull after the Care Center) -Nostalgia (this is a double-edged sword, as it's cool and fun to see the references, but at the same time it's used as a ----cheap gimmick and doesn't add much looking back on the game) -Graphics (easily one of the best-looking games I've played) -Gameplay (great)  That's about where the good ends. Again, it's a good game and I would recommend; I'm just disappointed.  Grace Parts 9/10 Leon Parts 6/10  Overall 7/10

As a lifelong veteran of the series whose very first video game was the original RE3 on the PS1, I can confidently say this is one of the best Resident Evil games ever made.  It features plenty of plot points and moments of blatant fan service, but they are handled so well that they feel incredibly fulfilling rather than cheap or incredulous. I loved the open exploration sections in a certain familiar location we’ve visited before as Leon, and I thoroughly enjoyed Grace’s sections in the Care Center, which captured that classic RE7 tension perfectly. In short, Capcom took everything that worked in the RE2 and RE4 remakes, RE7, and Village, and synthesized them into an amazing package. The pacing was also spot-on; it was just the right length to keep me fully engaged without ever getting burnt out or bored.  Admittedly, there were one or two narrative twists where I sat there thinking, "You must be joking, Capcom..." and a certain pharmaceutical company's ghost always seems to dig up yet another underground facility, no matter how many labs we watch go kaboom throughout the series. But those minor gripes aside, I stand by my verdict: this is easily one of the best Resident Evil games to date and deserves every accolade it gets. It is one of the few recent occasions where I didn't regret paying full price: I enjoyed every single minute.

The game is pretty good, i had a lot of fun & it was really damn good at setting the mood & atmosphere all the way throughout. Leon's Tense music was a pretty good choice, just wish they gave our boy a bit more beard. Grace's Move Speed is also pathetically slow outside the Tall girl chase. I REALLY don't like that Blister head's have an insta-kill grapple.  [h3] Grapple Breaking [/h3] I know RE2R, 3R AND 4R ALL featured a grapple break if you moved AWAY from an enemy with good timing, but in those games it was so short of a window that i wouldn't be surprised to find out the majority of players didn't even know it existed. In RE9, i think they struck a good balance, you take SOME damage instead of being completely unharmed, but it's SIGNIFICANTLY easier to do & the damage is almost nothing if you're only breaking away every now & then.  [h3] Difficulty [/h3] I believe the game is too forgiving when playing as GRACE after around 1hr in on STANDARD. Ammo drops & healing were so plentiful i started ignoring healing items because my item box had about 6 Med injectors. I think Leon's supply drop rates were fine. The GUN wielding zombies were stupid annoying though, very little wind-up & extremely likely to hit YOU but NOT their zombie buddies.  [h3] Useless? Light Switches [/h3] There are light switches in areas the Tall Girl cannot appear, i don't know what purpose it serves since the darkness doesn't appear to change gameplay outside of her confined zones. I don't know if this is cut content or deliberately done to make you THINK she can appear in those areas, either way, it's irrelevant on NG2+.  [h3] Forced Conflict [/h3] The Tall Girl has a couple of teleportation triggers that are impossible to believe, as in teleporting in front of you when she was seconds behind, it's almost as bad as FNAF Security Breach.  There are 3 Quartz Puzzles with Braille buttons & Either a (Sun, moon or Star) symbol above the buttons, the 3rd one REQUIRES the Blind girl's help because the icon images have faded AND the input displays are destroyed, but the Braille Remains. Remember that ALL 3 Quartz Puzzles have Braille on their buttons, so it is not impossible to realise which symbols the Braille Represents. I'm really just salty that the Devs didn't ALLOW for you to still do the puzzle, but create a failsafe trigger to continue the game basically as normal. Also there's a random horde fight here that has no reason to exist, you don't trigger an alarm or anything, yet for some reason enemies flood the area while you defend the blind girl.  [h3]New Game+ [/h3] Upon completing your 1st playthrough, the whole game changes FOREVER. Some cutscenes never play again & there is NO NG+. Instead, most unlocks are universally saved & can be collected from either the item box (Grace) or Item Shop (Leon).  In NG-2+, Leon gains the shop function from the beginning & worst of all, Leon can NEVER get weapons from the in-game world again, they can ONLY be obtained through the Shop. Even more fu**ed Up, there is a specific section of the game where you're SUPPOSED to use a sniper, Yes, it's technically possible without it, & the game even makes you an autosave BEFORE your purchase if you need to re-make your purchase, but it's still an upsetting realisation on your 2nd playthrough.  [h3] Replayability [/h3] Honestly, the game doesn't feel satisfying on subsequent playthroughs. It feels like the entire game is built around the expectation you will use the infinite gear & i think the fact the infinite gear is NOT locked behind insanity mode is the biggest flaw around this. There's also NOTHING to work towards unlocking.  [h3] Leon Must Die Forever [/h3] I'll keep it simple, this game mode is so lazy, most story-mode dialogue & items, were NOT removed from the game world. The giant red doors connecting map zones are an eye-sore. &, the music...never...changes.  [h3]The Final Puzzle[/h3] The puzzle itself is perfectly fine, it's obscure & fits the idea of a multi-session brainstorm for the community to come together & figure out the puzzle, unfortunately the reward is so pathetic it completely undermines ANY effort that went into it, & is single-handedly the 1 reason everyone unanimously hates it.

RE9 was one of my most anticipated games this year but despite having bought it on release, I only just finished it now after forcing myself to do so. The dual playstyles available in Requiem info prior to its release really had me excited but after playing the game, I think I might prefer doing one or the other. even though I think it works really well for Requiem. I know you can change this in the settings, but I wanted to play the game as intended with Grace in first-person and Leon in third-person.   Getting on with the review, I think with my hype having deflated in the time since its release, my overall impression is not as good as it would have been. Don't get me wrong, the game is fun but compared to 2 and 4 remake as well as 7, I'm not sure I would place requiem above any of those. There are really good moments in each part of the campaign but I don't think it does as well overall as the games above. It's weird and I'm at a loss at how to explain it.  With that said, what did I enjoy? Well, playing as Grace was a little rough at first until you get a bit of ammo and idea on how to play her vs Leon. I think I really enjoyed the way Grace was portrayed. She seems really anxious and has clearly gone through a lot before the events in-game and seeing how she develops is great. I was very much in Grace's corner with all the crap that happened and her sections are definitely terrifying and scratch the survival horror itch but I don't think they reach the highs you do in RE7 or the Ashley section in RE4.   As for Leon, it was such a good change of pace switching between them. The game felt like it took on a fresh coat of paint. Just annihilating enemies with the more experienced Leon was a blast and probably the reason why RE4R is one of my favorites in the series. The parry with the hatchet is brilliant and it always felt slick as hell to pull off, especially when I managed to do so with the later boss fights and certain enemies. But, the combat was not the only good part of Leon's campaign. The way it develops and the revisiting of Raccoon City and iconic locations within the series like the RPD really helped to characterize Leon's trajectory in the series. RE2R is probably my favorite remake in the series alongside 4 and I wish that the RPD section was a bit more fleshed out but its understandable why it wasn't given how it alongside the rest of the city has been in decay for close to 30 years. The game really did a good job pulling at my heartstrings with Leon's section especially towards the finale.   I think this dual narrative/gameplay style worked really well for the game because they chose to pair Grace up with an experienced vet like Leon. However, when I think of the gameplay in RE2R and 4R, it just feels perfectly tuned in a way that I didn't experience in Requiem and maybe that's nostalgia talking but I can't agree with others who think this game tops those. The other thing is how impressive the engine's visuals are. Path tracing and geometry detail in this game is insane. I hope they work on liquid stuff for subsequent games like Veronica and what not because it felt a bit low quality in comparison to rest of the objects in game. There's one part in the game after beating a boss where it melts kinda and its really obvious how at odds liquid objects are with the level of detail in the game elsewhere. Adding to this, the game runs well without any major issues at this time for me at least and that's something we need to really applaud in this day and age with all the UE5 stuff being shoved down our throats.  I'm really excited to see where the series goes next and the fact that there's going to be story DLC does have me hyped. I was extremely curious about the post-credits scenes and what/how other mainline characters like Chris, Claire, and Jill are doing in this timeline. I just really hope that Capcom remakes 0 and 1 as those are the only mainline games I still haven't tackled. Please CAPCOM!!!!!!!!! PLEASE!!!!!   Anyways, strong recommend. It's on sale now, so I would definitely grab it.

In short, it's pretty good, but I'm a bit mystified by the universal acclaim, and people saying this is the best entry. I thought Re:7, 9 and the 4 Remake were all vastly better, as well as the 2 and 3 remakes. Why? Cons: - It's very short (but full price, unlike RE3, which I completed after and is far better IMO)  - It appears to use a lot of reused assets/locations and mechanics/animations from the previous games. E.g. a certain location in Raccoon City, we've visited many, many times, and the animations and feel of the characters are very similar to those in the 4 Remake. It feels like they rushed development simply mashing together stuff from RE4 remake and other recent entries with some old familiar locations and themes they know people feel fondly about.   - It doesn't do anything new - unlike for example RE 7: Village, which contained loads of new ideas and was much more expansive, and RE 6: Biohazard which moved the series forward with first person perspective and really leaning into the story-telling opportunities this provided. This is not in any way a bold or novel game.  - The enemies are completely forgettable with little variation, and this is done better in the aforementioned games.  - While people rave about the return to survival horror, we're really talking about Grace's sections containing some bog standard/generic RE gameplay with limited ammo and the usual kind of puzzles we've seen so many times before.  - The Leon sections are cool, as they are really cinematic and make you feel "bad ass", but ultimately pretty simple game-play wise.   - The story was rather boring, and didn't grab me like the others. It's a remix of all the same fair we've been seeing since the original, without any exciting new twists. - The locations weren't very varied. There's basically only two locations and they're ones we've seen before - an old building/mansion (the hotel), and Raccoon City. It's important to say that RC is mostly just bland grey rubble and ruined streets. The RC in 2 and 3 Remake is much more interesting, limited though it still is.  - The weapons - with the exception of a certain fast spinning bladed weapon - are also generic.  - There's no real attempt to cache on on this semi open-world aspect of RC. It's basically a couple of blocks with some abandoned buildings, linked by a really janky motorbike section, which you can't actually control.   Pro's: There's lots of call backs to previous games - if that's your jam, you'll be pleased.  The Leon sections are "bad ass" as I've said, and the game does a good job of presenting an older grizzled version of the character. Graphics and sound design are excellent as usual.  Runs well on RTX 3080 at 1440p.  I appreciate that.  Conclusion: I strongly suspect that people who put this at the top tier of quality in terms of the recent entries, have heavy nostalgia for the original games, characters, and locations, which means they get something more from this than I. I played the original at the time, but it doesn't in any way thrill me to be back at (a blander post-apocalyptic) Raccoon City. I thought Nathan Winters was far more interesting than Leon, for example.  All that said, it's a decent game - it's just a big  step down from the other ones produced in the last decade or so. Therefore, I'm leaving a negative review, but it's still well worth playing and other people may feel very differently.  Rating 6/10.

Resident Evil Requiem feels like Capcom's "greatest hits" collection turned into a modern AAA horror game. It successfully blends the tense survival horror of older Resident Evil titles with the more action-focused gameplay popularized by Leon's recent adventures. Critics and players have praised its atmosphere, visuals, combat, puzzles, and dual-protagonist structure.  What works well  ✅ Excellent horror atmosphere – Dark environments, unsettling creatures, and constant tension make it one of the scariest recent entries.  ✅ Dual protagonists – Grace Ashcroft delivers classic survival-horror gameplay, while Leon Kennedy brings more action-oriented segments. The contrast keeps the pacing fresh.  ✅ Strong blend of old and new – Requiem balances exploration, puzzles, resource management, and action better than many previous entries.  ✅ Outstanding production values – The RE Engine continues to deliver some of the best graphics, facial animations, and environmental detail in the genre.  ✅ Fan service done right – Longtime fans will appreciate callbacks to Raccoon City and earlier games without the story becoming inaccessible to newcomers.

You know what I like about horror?  The moment people realize they're not in control.  Not the screaming. Not the monsters. That moment.  The exact second somebody understands the rules they trusted aren't protecting them anymore.  Resident Evil Requiem is built entirely around that feeling.  Every room feels contaminated by something you can't quite see. The walls look sick. The air feels wrong. The whole game carries itself like it knows something terrible and is enjoying the fact that you don't.  I respect that.  Most horror games throw monsters at you and hope you'll panic. This one is more patient. It lets the dread settle in. It lets your imagination do half the work. Every hallway becomes a question. Every door becomes a decision.  And eventually you stop wanting answers.  Because answers are usually worse.  The creatures are incredible. Not because they're powerful. Because they're unnatural. They look like mistakes that kept growing. Things that should have died long ago but somehow found reasons not to.  I couldn't stop staring at them.  The best horror isn't about danger.  It's about fascination.  The feeling that you should look away but don't.  The game understands that perfectly.  And then there's Raccoon City.  Or what's left of it.  Walking through those ruins feels like visiting the scene of a crime nobody ever solved. Every broken street, every ruined building, every abandoned corridor carrying the weight of disasters that never really ended.  It's beautiful.  In the same way a thunderstorm is beautiful.  Something destructive. Something inevitable.  By the end, I wasn't trying to escape anymore.  I was curious what the nightmare would show me next.  Elegant. Disturbing. Addictive.  A masterpiece that understands fear isn't about being chased by monsters.  It's about realizing the monsters have been waiting for you the whole time.

Requiem is an excellent edition to the RE franchise. It did an wonderful job of balancing the feel of new and old RE games, starting with having two playable main characters: new-entry Grace Ashcroft and fan-favorite Leon Kennedy. Unlike many of the previous RE games with a secondary character, time is split pretty evenly between the two protagonists.  Uniquely to this title, however, they also play very differently.  When you are in control of Grace, the game returns to its roots: a survival horror experience where you have limited supplies, the enemies are all much stronger than you, and you need to proceed with caution. She defaults to the first person perspective (like in RE 7 and 8), although you can change this in the settings. When you control Leon, on the other hand, you are an action hero playing in the 3rd person. You come equipped with significantly more--and better--gear and you have a massive inventory as opposed to Grace's piddling one. You can also buy better gear and improve your weapons as you go.  The creature design was excellent as well. We had some good returning creatures--looking at your lickers--but also some very cool new designs. This game was also unusual in that they decreased the number of boss fights where the boss had giant, glowing weak-points. I mean, they definitely still had them, but there were some bosses without them!   Two final notes I'd like to make in regards to performance and motion sickness.  [b] 1. Performance: [/b] I was surprised by how well this ran. While you can obviously manually change your settings whenever you feel like it, during initial setup the game will ask you if you prefer to emphasize performance or visuals and then automatically set your graphics based on that selection and your hardware. I thought the game did an excellent job doing this and the default graphical settings selected were much higher than I was excepting on my aging (and never top-tier) GPU. Framerate remained steady during my entire time with the game and my GPU/CPU temps never exceeded 60C.   [b] 2. Motion Sickness: [/b] Like many games, RE9 comes with some settings to help reduce motion sickness. They do help, but I still had some initial difficulty with the first-person perspective. It got a bit easier once I could run (rather than walk), as the motion seemed smoother. I did manage to play the entire game with the default perspectives (so Grace's parts were all first-person) so this was a surmountable challenge, but it is something to keep in mind if you are particularly prone to motion sickness in games.   This is an easy recommendation. Go buy it! Even at full price, it is worth it.

A lot of people will probably say that’s because Leon is finally back as the lead in a mainline entry, and for the most part, they’d be right. But there’s more to it than that.  This game builds on everything that made Resident Evil 4 Remake great while still finding ways to innovate and stay true to the series’ roots. My only real gripe, and I’ll keep this spoiler-free, is that it occasionally leans a little too hard on nostalgia. Certain characters are brought back in ways that can make the story feel a bit surreal. That’s not necessarily a bad thing, and their dramatic reappearances definitely deliver on the shock factor, but it felt a little forced at times.  Aside from that, the game is fantastic. The duality of the story and the way each area can be approached differently depending on who you’re playing keeps things fresh throughout. The gunplay is tight and responsive, and Leon has even more tricks up his sleeve than he did in RE4 Remake. Enemy variety is solid, and the horror elements are handled exceptionally well, especially during the early sections of the game, where the atmosphere and tension are at their strongest.  Overall, this is one of the most enjoyable Resident Evil experiences I’ve had in years,

I first played RE9 on Switch 2. I was apprehensive about playing it that way because I know the Switch 2 is a bit weak and I had a hard time believing I'd be able to experience the game in proper fashion. Funnily enough, it ran okay. Definitely had some framerate issues throughout, and ultimately it made the LMDF mode excessively hard to play. However, I enjoyed the game so much that I decided to pick it up here on Steam. It really is a great entry to the franchise, and it's unfortunate to see so many people confess such sour opinions on the game, especially regarding it's second half. While the Care Center is clearly the best portion of the game, I find the Raccoon City segment to be a great spiritual successor to RE4 in a lot of ways. The action is still really solid, despite what naysayers might lead you to believe.  I would be remiss if I didn't mention that one of RE9s best elements is it's new lead character. Grace is a great addition to the franchise, and I would be stoked to see her lead another game, perhaps one where she is the main focus, rather than dividing the game back and forth between her and Leon. I understand why Capcom took the dual-character approach here, it does work quite well, but I think Grace is a good enough character to where she could hold up a game of her own. Give her a bit more weapon diversity, and expand on the concepts executed in the Care Center and I think you have a recipe for another great RE title. As it stands, RE9 is great, and probably my favorite mainline RE game since RE4. I am eager to see what they deliver as it comes to DLC, and I hope that it is a step up from the Rose DLC for Village, as that was incredibly disappointing considering how much I actually enjoyed Village. I definitely have my gripes with the game as it pertains to the fate of some of it's characters, but it's RE through and through. Great work once again Capcom. 9 (heh) out of 10.

NOW WITH TALKING (AND SINGING) ZOMBIES! AND MORE [i]EXPLODING[/i] ENEMIES THAN EVER BEFORE!! (And after Capcom electing [i]not[/i] to put GIANT SPIDERS in the likes of RE2make for being too jarring to their present "aesthetic"...even [i]they[/i] seem to have somehow scuttered their welcome way back...)  Forget the Baker farmhouse, or the Village and its immediate surrounds: after the last two mainline RE games taking part in more rustic environs, this new chapter aptly brings us back to the more urban settings of RE2 and 3! Though we do begin in a place called Wrenwood, rather than Racoon City...      And we're initially, at least, playing a brand-new character in the franchise, a very green-seeming/previously-office-bound FBI agent named Grace...though I've a sneaking suspicion she may be related to someone from the I.P.'s past (like The Fast and the Furious movies, "family" is never far away in the RE universe)!  This said: the earliest portions of gameplay do feel quite a bit like RE7, and it's clear from the outset that our Grace [i]won't[/i] be a fighter, first and foremost (cue more glorious, terrifying, Outlast / Amnesia: The Bunker-style stealth-horror than ever before; and do expect to leave more zombies "alive", and needing to be constantly avoided, than ever before)! Good thing franchise fave Leon will [i]also[/i] be along for the rocky ride, soon enough. (Similarly, events will gradually move from the uber-spooky Wrenwood Hotel to a post-nuclear Racoon City - a brief visit to a super-dilapidated R.P.D. included, making this very much a homecoming/full circle proposition for Leon - by way of some other locations, of course, including classic horror mainstays like a hospital, a water treatment plant...and, yes, a small sewage facility, albeit one drained for once of all its water!!)  Character- and acting-wise - while it's still a long way from The Last of Us - we've come a long way since the days of "Watch out! It's a MONSTER!" and "Jill sandwiches". Grace is easily our most vulnerable-feeling RE protagonist ever: our first encounter with a freshly-transformed zombie being perhaps the most protracted and least action-hero-esque of the franchise (shy, perhaps, of our first meeting with Mia in RE7). So there's no doubt this one means to veer things seriously back in the horror-'n'-scares direction, after the thrilling-as-heck, yet far more action-oriented, Village...  Player perspective-wise is where things get [i]especially[/i] interesting. Just like the Winters' Expansion for Village, you can switch between first- and third-person POVs at any time...but the [i]default[/i] is first-person for the Grace bits, and third-person for the Leon bits. Which immediately sends the message home: as Grace, the scares definitely dominate - with much more limited resources to manage - while Leon's sections are going to be infinitely more mayhem-oriented! We're very much out to please [i]all[/i] manner of RE players here...and almost all [i]horror[/i] gamers, period...  Good thing it achieves these goals so well, then. Yup: after an in-my-opinion five-top-rate-mainline-games-in-a-row streak - yep, I'm one of "them" who champions even 3make - we're yet to take a single step down (sorry, RE6 fans: perhaps your shiz-slicked time will come again)! RE7, RE2make, RE3make, Village, RE4make...and now THIS! What ever did I do in a prior life to DESERVE ALL THIS GLORIOUSNESS?!  You can even, as Leon, seize the occasional chainsaw off a zombie and use it on [i]them[/i]; and if you're extra well-behaved, you may even earn yourself a chainsaw-versus-chainsaw battle as a bonus! Consider me an extremely happy chappy, and let's officially make that a [i]sixth[/i] 10/10 in a row (as long as you take out lazy, cheap-arsed side-crap like Resistance and Re:Verse...which I'm happy to utterly ignore the existence of)!!  Oh, and if I'm reading the figures right: the big Hollywood studios like Disney could [i]easily[/i] afford, like, multiple Tyrants and a shedload of Lickers? BETTER WATCH YOUR BACK, MARKIPLIER...  Verdict: 10/10. Personally I wouldn’t have minded a few more rural, gross real world adjacent locations a la 7, and less labs and mansions. The game does pull the R.P.D. card at some point, but you spend very little time there. Capcom should have made a meal out of that section. Resident Evil Requiem is a solid entry, and probably the most interesting Resident Evil story out of the recent games I played. It has strong atmosphere, great production values, and some excellent action gameplay, arguably even better-feeling than RE4 Remake in certain moments.  My main issue is the structure. The dual-protagonist setup did not fully work for me. Grace’s sections are easily the strongest part of the game: tense, atmospheric, investigative, and much closer to survival horror. I would honestly have preferred a longer Grace-only main campaign, with Leon’s side handled as a separate DLC in the style of Separate Ways.  Leon’s sections are fun, and the action feels great, but they are often too short to fully satisfy. The game gives you these strong bursts of excellent combat, then pulls away before you can really settle into that rhythm. As a result, the campaign sometimes feels like two shorter games stitched together rather than one fully coherent long game.  Still, the highs are very high. Grace is a great addition, the story is compelling, and the game has a stronger sense of mystery and narrative ambition than I expected from Resident Evil. It left me slightly frustrated because I could see an even better version of it inside the structure, but I still enjoyed the journey and would recommend it.

Recommended? Yes 👍  Resident Evil: Requiem is an absolute masterpiece. The developers completely knocked it out of the park with this entry, nailing the perfect balance between classic survival horror and pure action, all while delivering a level of performance that other recent releases can only dream of.  The absolute best part of the game is how the entire vibe changes depending on who you're playing as:  Grace (Pure Survival Horror): Playing as Grace forces you to play it safe and watch your step. It's not just about difficulty; the gameplay is explicitly designed to make you feel the weight of the past trauma she's reliving. The tension is suffocating, and every single corner keeps you on edge.  Leon (Brutal Action): On the flip side, you have Leon, who completely breaks the mold from previous games. This is a seasoned veteran who is thoroughly enjoying the brutal action he dishes out along the way. It’s fast, aggressive, and incredibly satisfying to play.  Nostalgia hits deep: Having key parts of the story take place in iconic locations like Raccoon City is an amazing gift for long-time fans of the franchise. Revisiting those streets with this level of detail is mind-blowing.  Flawless technical performance: Visually, the game is a total showstopper, but the real highlight is the insane optimization. It runs smooth as silk from day one, with zero stutters or weird frame drops. You can really tell the developers put massive effort and genuine care into polishing this engine; it’s refreshing to see a modern AAA game run this beautifully.  A flawless, well-rounded game. If you're a fan of the franchise, this is a must-buy.  Score: 10/10

As someone who is still pretty new to the Resident Evil franchise, having only played the remakes of 2, 3, and 4, along with a playthrough of Resident Evil 5 on the Xbox 360 years ago. I feel like Resident Evil Requiem does a great job of mixing and elevating both sides of the series' identity. On one hand, you have Grace's point of view, which delivers that classic Resident Evil survival horror vibe. On the other hand, you have our poster boy, Leon, bringing that modernized, action-style gameplay. These two styles act like a total yin and yang, which really keeps Requiem exciting, even if there are a few caveats.  The story kicks off by introducing a new character named Grace Ashcroft, an FBI intelligence analyst tasked with investigating the abandoned, partially burned-down Wrenwood Hotel. From there, you uncover the truth about Grace's past and see how it all ties into the main plot. The game introduces a dual-protagonist POV, which hasn't really been done this way before. You play certain segments as Grace, and then you switch over to Leon, whose action sequences were something I always looked forward to. Leon is a lot older now, if I remember correctly, he's around 50, making him way more mature and plagued by guilt over what happened 28 years ago. Another cool feature making its debut in RE9 is the ability to swap camera perspectives on the fly. It was recommended to play Grace's parts in first-person, but I couldn't do it because I was scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. On the downside, I found the plot a bit too predictable, and the dual-POV felt a little too skewed toward Grace for my liking. Grace's sections felt way longer, while Leon's were over before I knew it. That kind of sucked because I didn't really like Grace at first; honestly, I found her pretty incompetent and annoying. As the story went on, though, she did start to grow on me a bit.  After a while, you actually end up heading back to the city that started Leon's career. I won't name it because of spoilers, but if you've played the older games, you already know. It was awesome seeing it again after all this time, and Leon's flashbacks as he opened the doors were a really cool touch. Exploring the city was great, but I do feel like it was needlessly bloated with empty spaces and "fake" doors and rooms just to make it seem bigger than it actually is.  Overall, though, I had a blast with RE9. It successfully combined the vibes of RE2R and RE4R, taking both the survival horror and action horror elements to the next level. It definitely has its flaws, but there's no way I could call it a bad game, or even a bad Resident Evil game.

In my opinion easily one of the best Resident Evil games (also one of the best horror games). The Grace section when you first start exploring the wings of the Asylum is the craziest and most stressful experience I've had in a horror game. This means you'll run over an empty, enemy'less street to something you think you can interact with only to realise the space only exists to make the city feel more open.   - The enemies are so few and far between. Re 4 remake had such a great balance of action that would keep you low on your resources - here I never ran out of ammo. I think having a bigger area to explore for resources but not enough enemies to warrant that exploration felt counter-intuitive.   - The stagger system is still so annoying. [h1] A Real Love Letter To The Franchise [/h1]  [h3] Also My 100th Review On Steam [/h3]  Resident Evil Requiem is, in my opinion, the best Resident Evil game ever made. As someone who has been a long time fan of the franchise since getting the ‘Claire Disc’ from my uncle back in 2002 for the Play Station 1 for Resident Evil 2, I can confidently say that this game beats the Two Remake and Four Remake hands down.   Both of those other games are phenomenal in their own right but this one just incredible. Capcom have never been too solid on their storytelling, but with this combined with Pragmata we could be seeing a much stronger era in narratives from the developers.  RE9 mostly puts us in the shoes of Grace Ashcroft, daughter of Alyssa Ashcroft (Who you might remember as the journalist -lockpicker- from the Resident Evil: Outbreak spin off series), who is thrust into a conspiracy in the shadow of Umbrella and needs to make it out alive.  You will be familiar with her gameplay if you’ve enjoyed Resident Evil 7 & 8 (Village), as her missions take place in a first person point of view where you have minimal means to defend yourself and the game is far more survival horror. Where it is better to dodge and stealth around enemies than to actually try and take them head on.   And what I would also like to note about Grace is her character. For me it is so refreshing to have a character who is actually scared and aware of the things that are going on around her. She is terrified for 99% of this game and it’s so nice to see, even during the gameplay you can hear her scared breathing and her hands shaking, not just in cutscenes and then it’s back to a stone-faced gameplay performance. Utterly brilliant.  Leon, on the other hand, his part of the game takes on the role of exactly what you’d expect from the Resident Evil Franchise from 4-6. It’s a much more run and gun action survival horror than Grace’s missions. Although it would be difficult to convince an audience that Leon would really be scared of anything.  Playing as Leon is great, a strong change of pace from Grace’s narrative and it is so much fun to play. It’s definitely on par with the Resident Evil 4 Remake in terms of gameplay and of course he’s still as sassy as ever.  Throughout the game you will also notice that there are staples from other games which have crept their way in, just little nods to previous entries; a design choice here, a bit of dialogue there. A long term fan of the franchise will be able to pick up on these little references no problem and a newcomer to the series will simply enjoy them for what they are regardless.  Overall, Resident Evil Requiem is the best entry into the franchise, made with love and care from the development team at Capcom and I honestly struggle to see how they can top this going forward, as they might just have peaked.  10/10 – I’m glad I chose to hold off on playing this to make it my 100th Review on Steam.
