Reviewing (mostly) every game (or DLC) in my library, part 612:  ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆ (9/10)  I want to say the RE franchise is so back, but we've honestly never really left, even after the divisive RE3R. 7 and 8 are in my top RE games, so I view the RE games through a survival-horror lens instead of an action-heavy one. However, [i]Resident Evil Requiem[/i] has enough for both types of fans! I consider it a "greatest hits" collection, as it takes the best of RE2, 4R, 6, 7, and 8. The dual protagonists were something I was worried about (hi RE6), but RE9 has quickly solidified itself as a terrific game. What struck me, however, was how RE9 wasn't [i]innovative.[/i]   Now, I mean that as a good and bad thing! The best parts were all elements we've seen before: Grace's gameplay is a homage to old-school survival horror; "alive" zombies are present in [i]I Am Legend, Zombieland, The Walking Dead[/i], etc.; Leon's gameplay is "nostalgia bait," taking its setting from RE2 and its gameplay from 4R/6; and we've been chased by Mr. X/Nemesis/the Xenomorph. The thing is, though, this formula [i]works[/i]. RE has spent nearly three decades experimenting with what survival horror can look like, and RE9 feels like the result of that long trial-and-error process. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel so much as polish it. The game understands what makes Resident Evil tick—the tension of limited resources, the thrill of narrowly surviving an encounter, the uneasy balance between vulnerability and empowerment—and it leans into those strengths rather than chasing novelty for its own sake. Not to mention, Grace is an incredible protagonist, my favorite—yes, even above Leon/Chris/Jill/Ada. The atmosphere is one of the best: gloomy yet terrifying and beautiful. RE9 is not a perfect game, however. Leon's gameplay is a bit of a slog in the second half, and the familiar Racoon City ends up becoming dry and bland. His physicality doesn't feel as strong as in RE4. Lastly, while I love Leon as much as the next fan, I hope the next game will have a fresher face.  [b][h2]Pros:[/h2][/b] ✅[b] Grace.[/b] Grace is, quite frankly, one of the best RE protagonists created because she is uniquely human in a way the other protagonists are not. Jill, Leon, and Chris are superhuman agents who aren't phased by anything. Grace, in comparison, has honestly no business being in the field. Her anxiety and panic attacks are literally crippling, and I felt [i]awful[/i] listening to her gasps and cries as she ran away. But her weakness makes her incredibly relatable and actually gives RE some damn [i]emotion.[/i] Her screaming in the hotel and elevator scenes??? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, her VA deserves an award for that. You watch her grow as a person, too. You see her put on a brave face for Emily; you see her intelligence when she inputs the correct password; and you see her determination and bravery when she [spoiler]saves Leon's life when putting the gun to her head.[/spoiler] She becomes someone who acts despite fear. And I love her.  ✅[b] The Care Center.[/b] It's probably the most fun I've had as a first-time playthrough. I was always planning, figuring out who needed to be killed, trying out strategies to lure zombies out of certain areas. The horror and tension are much higher than usual, thanks to the atmosphere. The red danger lights, the tight corridors, how beautiful but chilling the Center is ... an incredible setting. I also found the blood crafting and hemolytic injector to be genius! I had to be extremely conservative with ammo, but being able to clear out a large portion of the Care Center with just the injector felt very satisfying. Needing blood to craft items led to such an interesting risk/reward balance as you’d have to decide when to use blood, if it’s worth trying to collect more, or if you should kill an enemy for their blood. Very much like [i]The Evil Within 2[/i]!  ✅[b] Zombies.[/b] The zombies during Grace's section are easily the best zombies there's ever been. Love the personalities and outfits. I don't like zombies that are ALIVE. I don’t like when they sing, turn off lights, mop, are sensitive to light, laugh, climb, apologize, DRIVE, or shoot weapons. They're supposed to be DEAD. Because what's more terrifying than the thought that a zombie retains some personality or memories?   ✅[b] [i] Requiem[/i] motif.[/b] Respectfully, the writing of the RE games has always been its weakest part, ranging from lazy conveniences, cheesy dialogue, and plot holes. The overarching conspiracy is the same old, same old. However, the writers actually found something coherent to say. Requiem, meaning: (especially in the Roman Catholic Church) a Mass for the repose of the souls of the dead. Or: an act or token of remembrance. Grace’s story is basically one long confrontation with her past. She goes back to the hotel where her mom was [spoiler]murdered[/spoiler]—no detours, no safety net. And when Leon gives her that Requiem—one bullet, one shot—it signals something final. Something meant to end things cleanly. Her drop into the basement to save Emily feels like hitting rock bottom, literally and emotionally. And when she finally turns the [spoiler]Requiem[/spoiler] on herself, it's a sign of bravery. Remember this! I also thought [spoiler]the password—HOPE, or Elpis—is a nice touch.[/spoiler] In the Pandora myth, hope is the last thing left after everything else is gone. That fits Grace perfectly. After all the fear, guilt, and trauma, that’s the one thing she still has to hold onto.  ➡️ [b]Leon’s side is similar. [/b]Going back to Raccoon City is excellent, the place where his life changed. It’s him facing everything he couldn’t fix. He’s more experienced now, but that doesn’t mean he’s over it. The tone around both characters is dark and gloomy, with a focus on their trauma. The story still has its usual RE nonsense, but the theme actually lands this time.   ✅[b] Great on Steam Deck.[/b] I dunno how Capcon does it with the RE games, but even with high settings, I got a solid 45 FPS throughout the game. Not bad at all!  [b][h2]Cons:[/h2][/b] 🟥[b] Leon's gameplay.[/b] *Ducks tomatoes*. Listen, his gameplay works well as a foil to Grace, I'm not denying that. When you're so tense playing as Grace, Leon's gameplay is an exhalation. The physicality of his game is great; zombies can pick up a spinning chainsaw, impale themselves on it, then get cut in half as Leon finishes them off. The new animations are great! His parrying mechanic is neat, too. However, it just pales in comparison to her campaign. The gray streets and the generic zombies in ash gray feel like a downgrade. The novelty quickly runs out when it basically all looks the same. I can't help but draw comparisons to RE4's better enemy variety and encounter designs. The movement, combat, and overall responsiveness feel much better in 4R. It feels like the Care Center and Raccoon City were made by two different teams.  🟥[b] The Orphanage segment. [/b] It's such a momentum killer, full of exposition and walking. Super unnecessary.  🟥[b] No Claire or Jill???[/b] Not even a crumb for Claire? Release them from the basement, Capcom! Apparently, Leon's connection to [spoiler]Sherry is more relevant than Claire's ... [/spoiler]Does Capcom hate women or something? Either woman could have perfectly replaced Leon! A fun game. Can't say one of the best RE games but close. There are a few issues in this game that prevent it from being among the best RE titles such as RE4, Village, RE2, RE7, RE3 (original), RE2:  -Gameplay inconsistency: Some people liked it. Being able to play an overpowered character and a timid surviving one is a nice touch; but the passages between them make the game inconsistent. It's like eating a chocolate and olive at the same time, just odd.  -Lackluster story: RE is not appreciated for its stories but this is nah. This is not even comparable to the atmospheric gothic horror and warlord type story in Village, crazy family story in RE7, espionage intrigue in RE1, and disruption of family/friendship bonds in RE2. It is not even comparable to sweet B movie cheesiness of RE4. The main villains of the game are not memorable, lackluster final boss fight and a Wesker copy blonde unimportant villain hurts the storyline.  The positives:  + Gameplay: Enemy variety is insane, their brains working in patterns and all zombies having some sort of obsession is a phenomenal idea for gameplay. Stalker variety is great. While other RE games are usually limited to one stalker, this game has around four, and except the Girl, they are not unkillable. 1st person/3rd person are both handled very well, overpowered Leon has some slick moves and Grace's first struggles in using a heavy weapon such as requiem is just handled really good.  + Performance: RE Engine is appreciated for its performance and it shows here. Mid-tier graphics card can easily play the game on RT and it can play Path Tracing even in 4K for non-top tier (e.g. 5090, 4090, 5080) high-end cards (albeit in DLSS performance).  + Graphics: Best graphics ever in a RE game. Hands down.  + Sound design: So good. But RE titles are always good in that regard.  + Level design: Again, something that RE titles are usually good at. But still, some levels are so well made, this may be the best one in terms of level design, especially the mansion and Racoon City (construction traversal was amazing).  Overall, it's an 8/10 for me.

A Cinematic High That Struggles with Momentum Overview: Resident Evil Requiem delivers one of the most gripping opening acts in the franchise's history. It masterfully hooks players with a thick, oppressive atmosphere and a story buildup that feels both fresh and nostalgic. However, as the journey through a ruined Raccoon City progresses, the experience becomes a tale of two halves. The Highs (Pros): Masterful Atmosphere: The first few hours are pure survival horror perfection. The environmental storytelling and lighting create a mood that is incredibly immersive. Cinematic Presentation: The game looks and feels like a big-budget horror film. The character models (especially Leon and Grace) and the seamless transitions between gameplay and cutscenes are top-tier. Strong Hook: The narrative mystery is established early and effectively, making it nearly impossible to put the controller down during the initial chapters. Pacing Shifts: The transition from slow-burn survival horror to action-heavy segments feels jarring. These sequences can become repetitive, stripping away the tension that made the opening so special.

Fighting and game play is phenomenal - interesting, surprising, shocking, emotional, and violent, just how we like our RE games. My laptop had a hard time performing well at 120 FPS, it was constantly overheating, so I had to cap a lot of the settings and play around with it to find my device's happy medium. This game has every aspect you could want: an emotional compelling story, intense, gory, violent action scenes and gameplay, and crazy fun puzzles to complete.   This is already my personal GOTY, and I know it will be for a lot of others too. Definitely play this if you love horror, the RE franchise, or both!!

This negative review doesn't mean the game is bad by any means! In fact, in my opinion it is 8.5/10 and if you are a fan of RE then it can be very fun at times.  Then why the negative review?  Because after 5 years of waiting after RE8 and 3 years of waiting after the last RE (RE4 Remake), and after so much hype about Requiem, this is certainly not the installment that we deserved to get. After all it brings a far worse experience than the bests in the series (RE2 Remake and RE7), and is only slightly better than RE3 Remake (which is one of the weakest in the recent installments).  But why isn't it good? Here is why and be cautious for slight spoilers:  The story is slow and uninteresting, and worst part about it is that the grand reveal at the end of the game is more like "What the F! Are you kidding me? That doesn't make sense!" rather than being a grand revelation! The new character, Grace is way more likable than Ethan (protagonist of 7 & 8), however you will never believe her as a FBI agent (or Analyst) and she is constantly making an annoying sound like she is trapped naked in the snow! which is like a sad and futile attempt of the devs to force you to think the situations are scary! which is not how things works in reality!  There are many situations that you are trapped with the scariest monsters of the game (the girl) which should be terrifying on paper but in action they become boring and unsatisfying. Mostly because of very scripted sequences that the game brings and the bad and linear level design, which makes you predict everything from a mile away! They probably borrowed the idea of The girl (a monster with the weakness against light) from Amnesia the Bunker, but instead of learning from the mentioned game to give randomness and unpredictive behavior to the monster and make it dislike the like but still be able to function inside the light they made its behavior 99% scripted and predictable and the fact that you can just hide in plain sight but under the protection of a lamp is ridiculous and kills all the tension!  Another really weird part of the game is its pacing. For instance it gives you the most powerful weapon in the game right from the very start (WTF!)! Or Leon and Grace get introduced to each other too soon in the game (I was expecting it to be a cool moment later in the game but it wasn't), or the gameplay of each character constantly gets interrupted and gets switched to the other character because the dev thought the game would be more cinematic this way, but I personally prefer RE2 style where you can play as 2 characters in 2 separate playthrough without constant interruption.  Another aspect of the game is variety. What I expect and need as a player from a good RE game is varied zombies and bosses (and ideally level design). The zombie variation is decent even though it could be a little bit more, but most of the bosse fights are more or less the same: there is one chunky dude that comes towards you and you shoot at it and move away, no different strategies, different behaviors, or no interaction with the levels are needed during the bossfights. But one of my biggest gameplay related issues with the game is how they decided to bring variety to the game. They mostly focused on setpieces like motorcycle chase, or running away from child monsters! or some really uncalled for sections with fighting against soldiers which tured the game into a third person military shooter (thank god that section was short), or the melee fight against the leader of the commandos which was super boring! I would just trade all of that for 20 more minute of normal RE style zombie hunting.  But what is hurful the most for me is what the game could have been instead of an average RE. There is a really well done section in the mid game (East Racoon city area) where it's like a miniscule semi-open world area (the area becomes really big with a lot of side areas to explore), with satisfying amount of zombies to shoot at and especially a well designed levels where the floor is glass! So if the game was 3-4 of these areas one after another then it would be a 10/10 RE for me (instead of all the additional crap and predictable cliche level design that it currently has).  I personally think the future of RE or survival horror in general is to shift towards semi-open world level design. We already seen how satisfying East Raccoon city level here was and in my opinion one of the best levels in all of the survival horror games was the first small town area in Evil Within 2. So my finger is crossed for seeing more of something like that in the future.

Resident Evil Requiem proves that Capcom perfectly understands what makes this franchise shine. The claustrophobic survival horror of RE7 and the thrilling action of RE4, split brilliantly between its two protagonists and perspectives.  The Best of Both Worlds Grace Ashcroft (First-Person): Playing as the FBI analyst, the game takes on a dense, investigative survival horror tone. Exploring the abandoned hotel in the iconic Raccoon City, especially the Care Center section delivers some of the tensest moments of the franchise.  Leon S. Kennedy (Third-Person): With the legend himself, the title shifts to the classic over-the-shoulder view, focusing on the high-adrenaline, polished action gameplay fans love.  Technical Excellence The sound design deserves a special shout-out the immersion is so flawless that just by listening to footsteps and ambient creaks, you can identify exactly what kind of threat is lurking around the next dark corner. Visually, the RE Engine continues to look stunning while remaining incredibly well-optimized for PC.  Verdict Resource management remains vital and every bullet counts. The contrast between the two gameplay styles keeps the pacing perfect, ensuring the experience never feels repetitive.  Rating: 10/10 — A true requiem for the dead and an incredible nightmare for the living.

Resident Evil Requiem is yet another fantastic, already legendary follow-up of its amazing series. It features some of the most frightening encounters of the entire series. These were moments as tense as I've rarely experienced before. It doesn't matter whether you're more like a horror or an action guy. This game manages to please fans of either genre.   RER initially focuses on a young FBI agent called Grace Ashcroft, an analyst sent to investigate a series of mysterious deaths amongst survivors of Racoon City, few decades after the 1998 disaster. Her short forensic search through the inside of a shuttered hotel only lasts a short while before she gets abducted by Victor Gideon, RER's main antagonist with a bloody, disfigured face wearing greasy goggles. He holds her captive inside the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center, a huge mansion-like building with a labyrinth of locked doors full of T-Virus-infected people, cooks trying to turn you into their next meal and so on.  The well-known legendary RE protagonist Leon S. Kennedy makes a long-awaited comeback in this latest chapter. Pulling up in a Porsche, whilst having strange bruising on his skin indicating he might be infected with some affliction possibly related to the T-Virus exposure, is the way he returns. The true, undeniable star of this latest release is clearly Ms. Ashcroft who is just an incredibly relatable human being. The way from being on the brink of a panic attack to becoming self-assured enough to be able to fight back was as captivating as it was spine-chilling.  Requiem allows us to alternate control between Grace and Leon at certain points of the story with the possibility to set the POV for either character and choose between 1st or 3rd person with the indication in the menu, which perspective is more suitable for the respective character. That's a very welcome feature. Grace's parts are the most hair-raising ones by a mile. Underequipped and under constant threat from bloodthirsty stalker ghouls liable to descend from the rafters at any time, Grace's journey to escape from the horror of Victor's hospital is one of pure survival horror keeping you hella thrilled and excited from start to finish.  Managing all the items is, once again, crucial to survive the horrors Grace and Leon have to push through. Searching every little corner for possible ammo, herbs increasing your health, items to sell  at supply boxes for CP, with which you can purchase new weapon and upgrades as well as making use of your ressources sparingly is absolutely key to make it through this game. Every single find can make a difference.  In addition to all of that, Grace moves so slowly that it makes the timing your careful crouch-walk to avoid alerting all the zombies a real exercise in pinpoint pathmaking, especially when you don't have a distraction tool in your inventory at that moment. All of this is done, while navigating through pools of blood with the possibility of hungry golems appearing behind a corner.  The details are just top notch. When using the first person perspective you can genuinely feel the impact and damage every single bullets causes and that really makes you realize that, indeed, every single bullet is precious as hell and can make a huge difference. Every hit shot tears the festering flesh off the zombie faces leaving eyeballs hanging off and blood spatter painting the walls in red.   All the blood of the zombies isn't just there for visual reasons. No, Grace can actively syringe up the infected blood with a valuable blood collector. The collected blood can be combined with other pieces of scrap to craft invaluable items such as medkits and single-use hemolytic injectors, which can be used to silently take out an enemy, after sneaking up on it from behind, by causing their body to swell up and explode in the most disgusting way imaginable. It can also be used to dispose of a body in order to prevent it from reanimating and mutating, which obviously always happens when you least expect it.  Whilst Grace's part is shaped by a stealth playstyle side and plently of silence, Leon's one on the other hand is full of violence. That is clearly felt after the initial switch to him from Grace, which broke the tension almost right away. Especially when using the 3rd person POV, all the bloody mess and slaughter is shown off very clearly and this allowed to mentally revert to my all-action Resident Evil 4 mode, nailing headshots and launching head-on attacks on the enemies with various melee weapons. Not only that, but early on in Leon's part you even to carve your way through zombie crowds by putting a running chainsaw through their freakin' stomachs. Mr. Kennedy's sections are always pretty fast-paced and hella gruesome. That's perfect for people just wanting to quickly push their way through without spending too much time thinking about how to avoid alerting enemies or how to silently neutralize them.  Furthermore, Leon has a very broad amount of weaponry available, so it's not like you have to complete the entire sections of his with just some standard weapons. From beefy shotguns to head-splitting sniper rifles (which have even more firepower, if you attach the BSAA Emblem Charm in exchange for dismantling your attached scope) Leon has all the options to make his journey as fun as possible. In case he still somehow gets bored, he can still pick up weaons dropped by killed enemies and toss it at another one nearby. Instead of having to resort to harvest blood samples to craft new items with, Leon is simply rewarded with a special currency for every kill that can be cashed in at de facto ATM's for useful weapon upgrades, extra ammo, body armour and so on.  Even though I really enjoyed Leon's part, I still wonder if his sections were a bit too extreme in regards to the level of violence and the amount of action compared to Grace. It was just a huge switch each and every time between the slow and steady playstyle of Grace, where you had to sneak around a lot and Leon's part, which partially was a run-and-gun splatterfest giving off Call of Duty vibes. Both characters' sections were enjoyable as hell individually, but the difference between them was like day and night. Having them blended together a bit more over the course of the story certainly wouldn’t have been the worst idea.  Resident Evil Requiem perfectly merges the stories of Grace Ashcroft and Leon S.Kennedy into an extremely enjoyable story allowing us to get immersed into our beloved, legendary Resident Evil world once again. It introduced us to a new, exciting figure and gave us the return of a true legend. Moreover, RER amped up the gore to a new stomach-turning standard and unleashed a new bloodythirsty, disgusting breed of zombie along with some incredibly intense boss fights. The difference between the two aforementioned playstyles was just too massive no matter how exciting they were independently from each other. Capcom surely could've been able to find a better balance, but that's just minor criticism. Anyway, from my first steps into its shadows all the way to the COD-like shootouts and action, Capcom's latest release just constantly kept me entertained and on the edge of my seat and eventually that’s what matters.

The peak of Resident Evil for me was the RE2 remake, it improved on the original game but kept the parts that made the franchise special (the option to have the original soundtrack was a huge bonus). Although these games have always been a little cheesy and poorly written (B-movie dialogue, unbelievable scenarios, etc), in the RE2 remake it really felt like the game had grown up, it was genuinely tense and scary and gothic.   It wouldn't be fair to say that Resident Evil Requiem is a bad game, it's obviously a top tier game in some ways and has many elements that work, but the atmosphere and gameplay that previously made the series interesting and enjoyable has been stripped from the most recent games (although it occasionally finds it's footing in this one when playing as Grace) and morphed into something more like the RE films. I  generally found the parts with Grace more engaging to playthrough, in contrast to the Leon sections which I found tedious to the point that I am struggling to finish the game. Revisiting Racoon city could have been quite profound if done in an more thoughtful way, but it quickly becomes a gimmick.  The recent games have sold very well, so I suppose that's what informs the direction of the franchise, and other people must enjoy the current style. I wouldn't recommend spending full price on this personally, if you like the style and feel of the original and remake games. It does have some interesting moments, especially in the first act and when playing as Grace. I hope they remake some of the older titles with the same atmosphere and maturity as the RE2 remake.

It have 2 main issues with this game, then some smaller ones.   You fight the same enemies the entire game, by the end of the game when you do encounter the "new" enemy. You immediately have two ways to instantly kill it. They don't get to be scary like they were in previous games, and you interact with them in basically the same way you do every other enemy, shooting them as Leon or sneaking by them with Grace.  The boss fights are so incredibly lackluster. There might be one FIGHT in the game. If the boss fights in REmake 2 or RE8 are UFC matches, the boss fights in this game are WWE. They feel so scripted and forced. I don't feel like i actually had any input. The one you get as Grace is literally just pull 4 levers then click your mouse a few times. As i replay the game i just feel like the boss fights are another little event, not something i should worry about and prepare for. Don't even get me started on Zeno. The ninth installment in the Resident Evil series. It sheds light on FBI analyst Grace Ashcroft and her ties to Umbrella Corporation, along with the post-apocalyptic events of Raccoon City after the explosion, featuring our all time favorite: Leon S. Kennedy.  Pros:   ● A great mix between horror & action. Unlike previous installments that were only tied to one, you can get the feel of both here. You get to transition between two characters:  1- Grace Ashcroft: solely focused on horror, limited resources and strategizing for approaching enemies in effective ways. Has limited defense and is easily vulnerable.  2- Leon S. Kennedy: Significantly capable, wide arsenal of weapons, great stopping power, melee attacks, counter attacks, a hatchet which you practically cheat with, it parries and stealth kills everyone/everything and doesn't break. Just sharpen it after a couple of uses & you're good to go.  They wanted you to feel a night & day difference when playing with both, and they absolutely succeeded in doing just that.  ● The combat system is better than ever. Knife stabbing, parrying, melee attacks with a huge variety of animations that can also rely on surrounding environment, counter attacks, stealth kills and cinematic finishers have all been implemented in the game. Combat feel has never been this rewarding in a RE game.   ● Expansive lore on many beloved RE characters. You'll find clues, letters and features to many characters that were once present in the resident evil timeline, which tied many things together and answered lots of questions. This made me appreciate the game even more as a loyal fan to the series.  Cons:  The game unfortunately felt rushed in many aspects:  ● Lack of Challenges. I was disappointed with the lack of challenges and achievements. Wished there were more to extend my playtime and add a level of complication/challenge to my gaming experience.  ● Lack of brain usage: every locked safe code was practically given, game excessively hints to everything. They included one long & stupid puzzle only in the form a challenge to complete for points, which is not essential for game progression. Including a bunch of small rewarding puzzles throughout the game could've been way better than choosing to add one so long and unessential half the players wouldn't even attempt to solve.  ● Lack of creativity. Much of the game Locations and enemies are exhausted ideas, it seems that Capcom can't get enough of mansions, sewers, Lickers, Tyrants and laboratories. I get that the lab sections are essential to the lore of the game, but not with simple layouts and rooms that felt empty, there could've been so much more detail put in the final location of the game. Yet it all felt like a lifeless location just to wrap things up and find the typical "override keys" to progress. The care center was also smaller than what we're used to, and way more simpler to maneuver through than RPD. It was way generous in space and stripped of that claustrophobic feel we enjoyed back at the police station.  ● Poor elite guards AI and Tyrant animation. I was surprised with the clunky movement and stiff behavior the soldiers had, once they move to take cover they stay frozen and you'll need to get closer and find them yourself. Fighting these guards is like shooting targets at the merchant's shooting range in RE4.   The Tyrant boss fight had all the weird stuff happening, his arm weirdly twists when lifting a car, and some cars can be seen floating mid-air when fighting him.  ● Again, unsuitable voice acting. Capcom has been doing this weird trend where they decide to choose a voice actor that is not suitable for the game character, and it's worse this time. Just like they messed up with Ada in RE4, they messed up again with Emily and Chloe, I don't think that assigning at least a 15 year old kid to voice is difficult nor affects the budget, so why mess it up? It's so annoying, feels artificial when listening to Emily, and it somehow eliminates the feeling of vulnerability you should fully feel when playing as Chloe.  All in all, this is still a win in anyone's book, it's not common for us to see this great mix of horror and action in one single game. You'll enjoy every second of it. Afterall, this is a strong GOTY contender right here and a new Resident Evil installment you'll definitely have a good time with.

Spoiler free review (standard classic): the game takes creative risks in regards to the pacing, crafting system, and other aspects compared to the recent previous releases. I personally like that you have two characters, when you get bored of one you can play the other (given enough progress).   On the downside, the game doesn't reward resource management very heavily for both characters. At a certain point, you can just shoot at everything with grace and be fine. Grace's campaign has a section that is very abrasive on the eyes in first person but fortunately you can switch to third person.   My biggest problem with the game by far though is that sometime around either grace getting to the basement or Leon in rpd, the game consistently tanks in frame rate for a non-obvious reason. I'm not sure what the fix is, if I can fix it but I was playing on a 1080ti.   I like Leon's pacing overall but I wish it had more levels similar to the opening of the game, fighting rooms after rooms of zombies was where the gameplay excelled the most in my opinion. I would still recommend conserving magnum ammo for certain points but you're also not missing much if you use it.   I'm feeling between an 8 to a 9 on this game, my opinion might grow more positively with time as it did with village.   Spoiled review: I doubt this will be the final main entry of the series although the game does feel as though it could be a requiem to the franchise. The game has a pretty good story, especially considering it’s a resident evil game and gets a lot of mileage out of the title + themes. Considering the canon ending, Elpis could be an honoring of humanity and the ending of bioterrorism.   I’m not sure how I feel about the alternate ending, it definitely made me emotional but it also feels kind of like a scrapped ending because a) victor doesn’t return at all b) there’s no final bossfight c) the game gives you the option to immediately go back and see the alternate ending.   The elite guards section as Leon was insanely aggravating, probably the most frustrating part for me. It is an interesting change of pace compared to fighting zombies and does provide an explanation for the boss fight but the gameplay is so slow paced and punishes mistakes too heavily in my opinion. I could just be making mistakes and making that section harder for myself though.   I also wasn’t a fan of how many boss fights aren’t super clear when they can and can’t be damaged (at least on the first playthrough). There’s multiple bosses that start off being immune to damage until the game tells you “engage with X boss” and that goes back to my comment of the game barely rewarding resource management.   I spent a lot of time focusing on my shortcomings but the game truly is very well-made. Many people have already stated the positives and I anticipate myself replaying the game many times. As a resident evil fan, the game is worth the price tag in my opinion but it’s inevitably going to go on sale. I think Requiem is another solid entry into the Resident Evil franchise, but it has a few issues here and there that might not matter to certain players but to me it mattered enough that I wouldn't consider Requiem to be great. The gameplay shifting significantly between Grace and Leon does a great job of keeping things interesting on your first playthrough, but it hurts the game's replay value of which there isn't a whole lot to begin with.  Grace's gameplay is basically RE2 remake with a similar focus on knee-capping enemies so they stumble and you can run past them saving ammo, only now you have an optional first person mode and melee attacks that don't do damage but hard knockdown enemies letting you either kill them with a knife or run past them. You of course need to stun the enemy first before you can melee them. Leon's sections are just RE4 remake but with an infinite knife that you have to sharpen to use and a wide assortment of cinematic finishers that save you ammo and look cool.  On my first playthrough I thought both characters were great, on my second and third I found myself dreading the Grace sections because she only has 2 guns at the beginning and loses one of them halfway through the game. Not only that, but Grace has a stalker-type enemy that shows up a few too many times and those stalker segments are such a slog on repeat playthroughs. Leon's segments I never got tired of, but even his gameplay is lacking a little bit especially if you compare it to the upgrade system from 4. The weapon balance in Leon's segments is much weaker, where in 4 every handgun was not only viable but had a unique trait that set them apart, here the starting handgun is outclassed by both of the other handguns present in the game. The starting SMG and Shotgun also suffer from similar issues, however the rifles are fairly competitive with each other thankfully.  [strike] Insanity difficulty is also one of the worst designed difficulties I've ever seen. Insanity is the post-game difficulty you unlock and the enemies are so unbelievably overtuned that it's not enjoyable at all. Enemies get so much health and stagger resist that you basically don't get to kick people anymore as Leon which sucks a lot of fun out of the game, not only that but since perfect parries give you a guaranteed kill without requiring you to deplete a health bar the game goes from Resident Evil to Sekiro Requiem where the most efficient way to kill things is to just parry them. Grace also gets one-shot from full health if she ever gets grabbed without a knife on hand. [/strike] After stepping away from the game for a few days and deciding to give insanity another try without infinite ammo, I can confidently say that insanity isn't nearly as bad as I made it out to be in my original review. The issue is you're going from (relatively) baby mode Standard into Ball Crusher 9000 Insanity where everything one-shots you as Grace and needs a small milita's worth of ammo to die / to be Sekiro parried by Leon. The barrier of entry is really high, but once you get over that barrier and really learn how the developers intend for you to navigate Insanity, it's actually rather enjoyable. I just wish I got to kick people more often as Leon.  Overall I wouldn't pay $70 for this, I pre-ordered it (I know, you can laugh at me I will cry about it later) off of GMG for just under $60 and I think that's a little more reasonable. However, due to how poor the replayability is in this one I do feel a little ripped off. Honestly Requiem makes me eager to replay RE4 remake more than anything else. It's by no means a bad game though, on the contrary I think it's actually really good. I only wish the game's replayability was better.

I’m honestly a bit torn about this game.  The opening hours were genuinely intense. However, as the story went on, the horror factor kind of faded for me. I even had to log off for a bit because it was a bit too intense for me).  Anywho, the Care Center section is absolutely one of the standout moments. The map design there is fantastic, the puzzles would make you go back and forth between places, and the enemies were the most frightening for me. The pacing in that segment is just...... chef’s kiss. The sound design also deserves a lot of praise. A horror game lives or dies by its audio, and this game really delivers. You can often tell what’s approaching you just from the sound cues alone, which adds a lot to the immersion.  But of course, no game is perfect. Here are drawbacks for me:  The game feels very front-loaded. They'll lure you in with the beginning but then there's hardly any elements of surprise as the plot thickens. Boss fights are also a bit underwhelming. There aren’t many, and most of them aren’t particularly memorable.   So after running around like a headless chicken trying to solve puzzles and escape the horrifying creatures for roughly 24 hours in total, I generally had a good time. It just didn’t fully maintain the same level of fear and excitement throughout and this game may not be one that I would go back to for a second or more runs. Resident Evil Requiem blends the best parts of the series into one cohesive experience. Grace’s care center section brings back that classic survival horror feel of tight spaces, limited resources, and real tension. While Leon’s Raccoon City segments go full cinematic and are easily the highlight. The contrast between the two styles keeps the game fresh the whole way through.  Gameplay sticks to core Resident Evil mechanics with some nice additions. Sharpening Leon’s axe mid-fight adds tension, the Requiem gun is a fun new tool, and the puzzles (especially the blood sample ones) are actually engaging. The story delivers without falling flat, the ending is satisfying, and the game balances horror and action better than most entries.  Performance-wise, the RE Engine is as optimized as ever, and the inclusion of FS3 frame generation is a big plus. Overall, it feels like a mix of Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 4, and Resident Evil Village done right.

A Masterpiece of Survival Horror... When It Doesn't Crash! 😅  As someone who just finished streaming this entire game for my channel (clocking in at around 27 hours), I can confidently say Resident Evil Requiem is a massive win for the franchise. Capcom beautifully balanced pure, sweat-inducing survival horror with satisfying action.  Full playlist of the stream -- https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_RJ-1PSjCSM67ZkKwR82dPXjBowSykf7  The Good: The dual-protagonist system is brilliant. Playing as Grace Ashcroft gave me some of the most intense anxiety I've felt in a horror game in years—especially that insane segment escaping Gideon's House with only ONE bullet! It forces you to play smart and utilize stealth. On the flip side, switching to Leon S. Kennedy feels incredibly rewarding. After running and hiding as Grace, raiding the 3rd-floor office as Leon and dropping mutants with his classic combat style felt like the ultimate payback.  The atmosphere in the Raccoon City ruins and the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center is top-tier. The storyline involving Victor Gideon and protecting the blind girl (Emily/Elpis) kept me hooked until the very end.  The Bad (Technical Warning): I have to deduct some points for PC stability. Right in the middle of a tense underground cave section, an NVIDIA driver update somehow corrupted my game files, forcing me to do a complete reinstall from scratch. It was a nightmare for a live streamer!  Verdict: Technical hiccups aside, the game itself is phenomenal. If you are an RE fan, returning to the roots of the Raccoon City tragedy is an absolute must-play. Just do yourself a favor: update your GPU drivers before you start your playthrough!  Rating: Solid 9/10 (Would be a 10 if not for the driver crash!)

As a Resident Evil Fan since I played RE2 on my OG playstation back in the 90's, this game hit me with nostalgia like I've never experienced. From saving with an ink ribbon at a typewriter, crafting heals, making the decision to shoot or run depending on how many, or how few, bullets I have. Everything about this game hit all of the right notes. It's terrifying as Grace in FPS mode, it's awesome kicking-ass as Leon in TPP, all around, it was just super fun to play and even my fiance enjoyed laying next to me and helping us navigate creepy garages, dungeons, hallways and subway stations looking for a way forward. If you even remotely like Resident Evil, this is a must play.   That said, it's not perfect. The puzzles could be much harder (they're really easy). Bullets are plentiful (for the most part, much more so than OG RE/RE2). Grace gasps every 3 seconds and its super annoying. And the story is about as out of this world as you'd expect from Capcom (I'd love a storyline grounded in some sort of reality, but that's not really RE's thing). But in the grand scheme of things, it was a phenomenal game. There's plenty of reason to jump back in and play through the story again, and I'm looking forward to starting again... Maybe on insanity this time.

He is by far my favourite RE villain to date. He's ominous not because of his appearance, or how powerful he is, but his tone. It's threatening, but somehow friendly at the same time. He has a somewhat theatrical personality which really reminds me of Heath Ledger's Joker in TDK.   The voice acting for Victor but especially Grace is genuinely incredible too and yes, Leon is just as much of a cornball with his one liners as ever.  Overall it's an amazing game and I can't wait to see what the DLC's have in store for us.

There really isn't too much to say that already has been said. Resident Evil: Requiem is a lovely new entry into Capcom's believed survival-horror series.  And while I do rate this positively, I did have some gripes with the game. Namely, I feel the story beats just fall flat the farther in the game you get.  The game seems to rely a lot on nostalgia for getting a rise out of the player and bringing them joy in their playthrough (I don't necessarily think this is all completely bad. However, I found some of it well done while other parts of Capcom feeding into the nostalgia to be too on the nose). However, the biggest issue I had was how the game was split. What stood out the most to me is how well the game manages to capture the spirit of the older survival horror entries while still feeling modern in the way it plays. It really feels like the developers tried to bring back that balance between exploration, tension, and resource management that made the earlier titles so memorable, the story is told in a gradual way and doesn’t immediately explain everything to the player, which honestly makes it much more engaging. Very early on, the game sets up a mystery around the events that happened before you arrive, as you progress, you slowly uncover pieces of information through the environments, documents you find, and certain interactions with characters. It encourages the player to pay attention and connect the dots themselves rather than just giving all the answers right away, without going into spoilers, the narrative stays very faithful to the classic themes that have always defined the series. You still get that sense of dangerous experiments, situations spiraling out of control, and the consequences that come with people trying to push science too far, there are also several references to elements longtime fans will recognize, but they are integrated naturally and don’t feel forced. If you’ve played previous entries in the franchise, there are a few moments that quietly acknowledge the past without relying entirely on nostalgia, the characters are also quite well handled, at first, it’s not always clear what everyone’s motivations are, which adds a layer of uncertainty to the story, as the game progresses, you begin to understand them better, and that slow reveal keeps you curious about what will happen next, atmosphere is easily one of the strongest aspects of the game, the environments are extremely detailed and often feel oppressive in the best way possible, many of the locations feel like places with a real history behind them, and small environmental details hint at what might have happened before the player arrived. It really adds to the immersion and makes exploration rewarding, the game also does a great job at building tension, there are plenty of moments where you move slowly through an area simply because you’re not sure what might be waiting around the next corner. Sometimes even hearing a distant sound in another room is enough to make you stop and think before moving forward, that kind of atmosphere strongly reminds me of the older entries that focused more on suspense and dread rather than constant action, gameplay wise, it sticks closely to the survival horror formula, resources are limited, so every bullet matters, you often have to decide whether it’s worth fighting an enemy or if it’s smarter to avoid them and save your ammo. Inventory management also plays an important role since you can’t carry everything you find, that forces you to plan ahead and think carefully about what you bring with you, puzzles are present throughout the game as well, and they’re implemented nicely, they’re not overly complicated, but they still require observation and a bit of thought, some of them also encourage you to revisit areas after finding certain items or clues elsewhere, which makes exploration feel more interconnected, from a technical perspective, the game looks great, the environments are highly detailed, and the lighting especially stands out in darker areas where shadows and limited visibility play a big role in the atmosphere, the creature designs are also very well done and sometimes genuinely unsettling, sound design deserves a lot of credit too, footsteps, distant noises, creaking doors, and subtle background sounds all contribute to the constant feeling of tension, of course, it’s not completely perfect, there are a few moments that lean a bit more toward action compared to the rest of the experience, which can slightly break the slower survival horror pacing if you prefer the more suspenseful sections, enemy AI can also behave a little strangely on rare occasions, but it’s nothing that seriously affects the overall experience, even with those minor flaws, the overall experience is extremely solid, the atmosphere is excellent, exploration feels rewarding, and the story keeps you interested without revealing everything too quickly, you can clearly feel the influence of the older titles while still benefiting from modern gameplay and presentation, for longtime fans of the series, there’s a lot here to appreciate, and even for someone who is newer to this type of survival horror experience, it’s still a very strong and memorable game :)

For reference, I'm an RE fan and I love the series, but I can also critically analyze games. My top 3 RE games prior to Requiem are RE1 Remake, RE4 Remake, and RE5. Hopefully that helps you decide if my opinion is worth anything.  TLDR: Positive: Story, Characters, Environments, Music, Gameplay, Fan Service, Graphics, Community Puzzle Negative: Inputs, Weapons, Grey UI, Replayability  FULL: Let's start with the positive (and there's a lot of it) - The story is great, it had me up way past my bed time, it made me feel happy, sad, and made my jaw drop on at least two occasions. - The characters are amazing. Victor Gideon was incredible all the way through. I felt attached to Grace, and her interactions with everyone she meets really feels authentic for someone who is just a desk worker. I dislike young children in games, but I have to say Emily was handled very well and didn't annoy me. I don't need to say anything about Leon, right? Always my GOAT. - The environments are mostly excellent, the care center is 10/10 for sure. Raccoon City has a little bit of poor level design in places, but on my second play through I warmed up to it a bit more. - The music is very fitting and really sets the tone in every scene. The tense atmospheric music for Grace (especially in the final area), and the fact that Raccoon City really makes you feel like you're in a desolate wasteland, are a few notable examples. - The gameplay was, for the most part, really good. I wasn't sure how well the whole interweaving play styles would work but they really nailed it. The Grace sections feel tense with limited inventory space and the classic labyrinthine environments, with mechanics designed to keep you on your toes. And the Leon sections feel empowering with fast paced action which, although it doesn't quite hit the peaks of RE4 Remake, feels good nonetheless, and a few really fun set pieces to tackle. - The fan service is 10/10. If you love Resident Evil you'll love a LOT of the throwbacks and easter eggs in this game, they put a lot of effort in to appeasing fans of the series and it really shows. - The graphics are mostly gorgeous. I love how far the RE Engine has come in some ways, hair strands for example. Only a real stickler would have issues with the visuals of the environments and the characters. - "The Final Puzzle" was an excellent idea, it was incredible seeing the community come together to figure it out.  Now for the bad parts: - Inputs feel a bit clunky in places; especially noticeable at ladders in third person - you can literally run circles around a ladder without climbing it sometimes. There's some occasional random stopping if you change inputs while walking, and the removal of auto-firing for weapons like handguns from RE4R is a bit awkward too. - The weapons and weapon customization box are a big step down compared to RE4R. The completely grey UI is an eyesore, the upgrade system is a bit confusing to look at, and the weapon selection is a bit lacklustre. If you loved RE4R's weapons and merchant, this will probably be a disappointment for you. - The grey UI hits again with Leon's attache case - it's genuinely difficult to tell which items are which at a glance. There's even a mod for this to add color to the menu since this is a nightmare in terms of accessibility. - Replayability is a bit low if you don't add your own self-imposed challenges. There are fewer challenges to do compared to RE4R, and the lack of ranking system is an absolute shame. Nothing felt better than nailing that S+ rank, but they just got rid of it entirely.  Overall, this is an excellent game and I'm really happy with it despite a few notable flaws.  I'd give it a solid 8.5 or 9 out of 10.

[h3] 8/10 [/h3]  Resident Evil 9 has some really high quality aspects about it, but unfortunately it was only enough to create a good game, not a great game. I wouldn't say there's anything downright awful, there is a lot of quality, but i wouldn't say there's anything really exceptional either.  [h3] The Good: [/h3]  [b] -Graphics/Animations [/b] Ignoring the fact that i had to go under Resident Evil 9's config to change image quality, and most people had to download mods to disable film grain. Don't ask me why you cant change these things under settings. I gotta say though the graphics are really nice, probably one of the few exceptions in this game. Everything is really detailed and flushed out, they did a really good job designing them. It also seems optimized pretty well too, I'm not a fan of using cheap tricks to make it run better, but after doing a bit of fine tuning you can get this game looking really good. The animations are really stunning, CAPCOM hasn't lost their touch. They play a huge role in the graphics and gameplay. They almost completely carry the combat, getting grabbed, shooting limbs, running around. Just running into walls and opening doors is so much more immersive because of the animations.  [b] -Dynamic Duo [/b] Leon and Grace, These two characters pretty much carry the whole game, there isn't much else going for this game. They make up the whole narrative, and really make the story they're in. The writing and dialogue are done really well for these two, it never feels like they break character. I also really liked the idea of switching between these two characters, its a really good idea. For story purposes its really cool, its like playing the knight, and then playing the princess. In theory this sounds like a really cool concept and should technically work, but i think it kind of threw the gameplay off a bit.  [h3] The bad: [/h3]  [b] -Gameplay [/b] Resident Evil 9 really lacks the Resident Evil aspects. The only real gameplay mechanics there are in this game are the combat and sneaking, which unfortunately the sneaking is butchered in the first few hours of play. Starting out as Grace is actually really cool, you start with nothing and start exploring this care center which is almost like a castle. All the enemies seem really unique and dangerous, you don't really want to interact with them so you're sneaking past them, making distractions, until you run across a gun on the floor. This is where the gameplay for grace is really ruined. Adding combat for grace just completely destroys the sneaking mechanic, there just isn't a real reason for it anymore, you can pretty much kill every enemy in the game. The big problem with this isn't the combat either, like what's wrong with Grace running around and killing every enemy? The problem is the sneaking made the player focus on the world and enemies (IMMERSION) A game needs more then just running and shooting, the problem with RE9 is it doesn't really have any other gameplay. There are pretty much no puzzles other then having to get key to open door, which like is that even a puzzle? There almost isn't any world interaction, so there really is no point in looking around or exploring, other then just loot. The care center at least had a main objective so it made exploring it a little more interesting, it actually felt like Grace was trying to find something. After the care center though things really fall flat, it just kind of feels like you're trying to get the game over with, there's almost no exploring after the care center, like why would there be, there isn't anything to find. They should of made the world a lot bigger, added tons of puzzles, added other gameplay mechanics like some type of world interaction (IMMERSION) They also should of completely made Grace's gameplay just sneaking and exploring, throwing bottles is fine, they also should of added more distraction options, like guys you couldn't think past a bottle? Leon's gameplay kind of suffers from the same aspects, its less so because it really is just all about shooting and running, it actually felt like Leon's sections were built around his gameplay, Grace's sections felt more like Leon's action just bled into her gameplay which wasn't supposed to be there. Leon's gameplay still needed a lot more world interaction and puzzles. Like it would of been really cool if there were these puzzles you found and couldn't solve as Grace just yet, but when you switched to Leon you found the other pieces. Like just do something like that, it would of been way more interesting to play Leon or Grace. The coolest thing in the game is the parlor, that's about all the world interaction you get.  [b] -Going Small [/b] I think going small kind of messed with the gameplay, they had huge ideas, big plays, but never really went anywhere with them. Like the world interaction and puzzles, are they there? ya technically they are, but they're so dumbed down they're pretty much non existence. Almost every aspect of this game is dumbed down. Like for an example, the Chef, the first interaction is really cool, then they have him walking through hallways. Like guys make something out of him! Make a boss fight for Leon, or make a freezer area where you're hiding from him as Grace, do something more with him! Its not inherently bad, nothing is in this game, but they really just didn't use what they had. Everything, the whole game could of been so much more. This aspect bleeds into the story too. This game is very undeserving of it's overwhlemingly positive rating. This review will be as spoiler free as I can make it.  1. Everything is so sluggish. Movement feels low compared to previous games and it's way more noticable in Leon's sections. Animations during combat are way too long and the camera swings can be jarring. The low FOV that can't be changed makes this worse.  2. Combat feels horribly balanced with easy enemy parries in Leon's sections. Enemy variety is non-existent and almost all of them are ammo sponges. Sometimes a blister head can take 3 shotgun shells point blank and still not stun on normal difficulty. Boss design is terrible. You can just tank hits while you mag dump. I killed Leon's 4th boss without moving and I don't think a single boss fight lasts longer than 90s. They completely failed to remake RE4R combat.  3. Grace's gameplay is similar to RE7 as it focuses more on the horror elements. I think this is the best part of the game however none of the enemies feel like they pose a threat. There are too many healing items in this section on normal so you can simply tank attacks and walk past enemies without being punished. The GIrl also immediately loses aggro if she touches light and is way too predictable. Jumpsaces every 20s get old very fast.  4. Pacing sucks. Intro is took long and some segments are slogs to get through. The Raccoon City wasteland is probably the worst offender. There is no enemy variety besides weak zombie and bigger zombie that acts the same way. After arriving to RPD there is another godawful section where you have to control a helpless character and hide from NPCs. The segement doesn't event reveal anything that wasn't already implied moments before it.  5. Replayability seems very poor mainly due to the parts I mentioned above about poor pacing. The orphanage really is that ♥♥♥♥.  6. Weapon design is boring. Grace gets a pistol, a better pistol, and the requiem(mag). One pistol is just a straight upgrade over the other. The requiem is pointless for her. I didn't use it a single time and just left it in the itembox because the game was already easy. Leon's weapons all feel like they fire and ADS too slowly to start. None of them felt fun to use except for the semi auto sniper with the scope removed. There's also only 2 of each weapon type in the first playthrough which is a big step down in variety.  7. Plot sucks in the second half. It just feels like fan service and a story that's been shoehorned in.   I give the game a 3.5/10. I think the first half with Grace is decent survival horror once you get to the care center. Once you leave though the rest of the game drops off a cliff in terms of quality. I'd say the first half is a 7.5/10 and the second half is a 2/10. It's a bad game but not in a way that makes it funny.

[h3] Resident Evil Doesn't Miss. Happy 30th Anniversary! [/h3]   [b] TL:DR: [/b] Capcom went to the kitchen and started cooking with the 30th Anniversary of Resident Evil. Great story, characters, gameplay, and attention to detail make this installment one of the best in the series thus far imo. (9.5/10).  [b] Story: [/b] You play as Grace Ashford, an FBI analyst and daughter of Alyssa Ashford, who gets appointed to go on a mission to investigate random deaths that are linked to the Raccoon City incident. She comes across the Wrenwood hotel [spoiler] where her mother was murdered [/spoiler] and ends up getting abducted by none other than, Victor Gideon, (a former Umbrella employee). The FBI sending a technical analyst, especially one with trauma to investigate such a case is peak Resident Evil logic, so don't question it. Victor Gideon wanted Grace since she could be a key factor to obtaining something known as Elpis.   [b] Story Part 2: [/b] Later on in the story, Grace thought it was a great idea to part ways from Leon and gets abducted [b] again [/b] by Zeno (Albert Wesker at home) for her to reveal a password to unlock Elpis. This is the main motive for both Victor and Zeno, the two baddies (bad guys) in the story. Leon smexy ass Kennedy and his emo hairline at the ripe young age of 49 ends up stumbling upon this case and the battle of bio-organic terrorism/weaponry ensues. The game answers important questions such as Umbrella's whereabouts, the primary cause of the thermobaric missile on Raccoon City, and the importance of Oswell Spencer's role in the story which can contribute to fan-service. The game also brings back some old names/places that contributes to fan-service as well.  [b] Grace Ashford: [/b] Grace gets a lot of bad rep in this community. Hell, I understand why, but she has her moments in the story. As annoying as Grace was in this game's former sections, she kinda grew on me in the latter half. She is this blubbering mess of a person in the beginning that constantly stutters, but when she comes across Emily, a little girl being experimented on by Victor, she ends up having character growth. She pulls herself together for Emily's safety and well-being; realizing she can't be afraid as she was in the beginning cause someone else depends on her for protection.  [b] Leon Kennedy: [/b] Leon Kennedy is back to deliver cheesy one-liners and deliver justice where justice is due. They have no right to make Leon this hot. Eck hem (excuse me). On a more serious note, we dive into Leon's past trauma from the Raccoon City incident. He recalls witnessing how average day citizens were being impacted negatively by the release of BOWs such as the t-virus. This is especially heart breaking since he was completely oblivious to the thought of a thermobaric missile heading their way at the time. Not being unable to rescue the residents in Raccoon City and finding out that the place he and others called home struck several nerves. Following this, he wants to stop the production of BOWs and to put an end to Umbrella once and for all.   [b] Gameplay: [/b] Capcom in their infinite wisdom has had [b] enough [/b] with the constant pandering to one particular audience, so they just decided to cram two different genres in one game. The game appeals to both the survival horror and action horror fanbases. Grace Ashcroft's section of the game is more survival horror centric and Leon's is more action horror centric. Grace's section has more of a fear factor with isolation, inventory management, and undergoing nerve-racking situations due to her lack of experience dealing with bio-organic weapons (B.O.W.). On the contrary, Leon's sections feel more action packed due to Leon's experience and professionalism when handling BOW's. The game is around 10-14 hours long for a first playthrough and has a whole assortment of things to grind for just like the older games (i.e. infinite ammo, new cosmetics, guns, etc.).   [b] Crafting: [/b] Crafting makes a return and has thus been a stable for modern RE games. Grace obtains items by sticking a syringe up a zombie's ass to obtain blood samples while Leon obtains items by buying them off of a computer. Leon's crafting is understandable since where he is during the game, scrap is easily obtainable. In Grace's crafting scheme, how does one make scrap out of blood samples, let alone ammunition? Screw being an FBI analyst, she should be in the lab with Rebecca Chambers.   [b] Gunplay: [/b] The gunplay in this game is some of the best in the series. All the guns feel as powerful as they should be with the shells and reloads being ASMR material. The guns are handled by both characters differently and tie together to their  overall experience and skill-level out on the field. Leon, obviously being the more experienced one, can aim faster, check his guns, sharpen his axe, and has much better recoil control compared to Grace, especially with big guns like the requiem (yes, one of the guns is named after the game's title). Grace in particular develops better gun discipline and better overall combat awareness later in the game and this is noticeable by her aiming faster in the latter half of the story and kicking zombies instead of giving them a little push.   [b] Violence: [/b] I don't want to come of as sadistic, but Capcom, don't be afraid to increase the gore in the Resident Evil games. They're M rated games for a reason. Thankfully, the blood and gore in this game is amped up drastically compared to previous games like RE8 and RE3 remake with an addition to enemy physics. This is a change I adore since I was disappointed in the lack of gore in RE3 remake and even RE8, but RE9 fixed that while adding more to it. In RE9, when you shoot something with a big gun like the requiem, it [b] looks [/b] like you shot it with that gun. When you kill something, a pool of blood forms underneath. When you kick an enemy down a stair case, they fall all the way down the steps and hit the wall. Not to mention the death scenes can be brutal, especially for the faint of heart.   [b] Overall: [/b] Once again, Capcom proves once again that they can indeed cook with the Resident Evil series. Everything from the graphics, replayability, story, and overall care for the game is exceptionally well thought out. This game is a possible contender for 2026 game of the year no doubt. Happy 30th anniversary Resident Evil!  [b] Rating: [/b] 9.5/10

Resident Evil Requiem – A Terrifying Return to Survival Horror  If you’re a fan of survival horror, Resident Evil Requiem delivers a gripping experience that truly lives up to the legacy of the series. From the moment you step into the abandoned Umbrella facilities and the eerily quiet corridors of the Orphanage, the game keeps you on edge with a perfect balance of tension, jump scares, and psychological horror.  The story is surprisingly deep for a modern RE title. It weaves together the fates of both new and familiar characters, revealing the dark experiments of Umbrella in ways that feel both fresh and satisfying. Every note, audio log, and hidden document adds layers to the narrative, making exploration feel rewarding.  Gameplay-wise, Requiem excels in pacing. It mixes classic survival mechanics — limited ammo, tight inventory management, and clever puzzle-solving — with intense encounters that genuinely scare you. The AI of enemies, especially the orphanage children and the Umbrella monsters, is unsettlingly effective, creating moments where stealth and strategy are just as crucial as reflexes.  Visually and atmospherically, the game shines. The dim lighting, realistic sound design, and haunting music combine to create an immersive horror experience. There were multiple times I found myself holding my breath, just hoping the next corner wouldn’t reveal something horrific.  In short, Resident Evil Requiem isn’t just another RE title — it’s a love letter to fans of survival horror. With a compelling story, terrifying encounters, and a suspenseful atmosphere, it proves that the series still knows how to scare, thrill, and keep you hooked until the very end. Another amazing entry in Resident Evil saga. It was always a point of discussion, action vs horror, and how true RE game should feel. Now they have found great middle ground. Gameplaywise:  Grace's levels feel like pure horror, watching out for enemies, managing inventory, stealth, survival, and making best out of the situation. Certain enemies can be manipulated (eg. zombie that has OCD(?) that you can turn on the light so he will run to turn it off, and genuinely marvelous design throughout the entire game. Leon's levels are pure horror, but you're the horror. Shooting enemies in the leg, roundhouse kicking them, finishing them with axe, and certain contextual kills really make you feel like Zombie Killing Machine. So if you are chasing only ONE of these playstyles, you might be bit frustrated with certain levels, as I was, simply wanting to kick ass as Leon instead of Grace's slow and deliberate playstyle and levels. But pacing in this is genuinely amazing (if you do not get stuck!).  Going through level with Grace being scared and then playing with Leon and swiping enemies creates amazing cathartic feeling. However, if you want entire game to be action - go for Village or RE4. And if you want survival horror - RE2, RE7 are better choice (Silent Hill 2,*cough, cough*). But, if you want Resident Evil: Best Hits - this is the one. Best of both worlds. Performance wise 10/10, nothing to add, genuinely one of the best looking games out there while running smooth as a butter. Storywise, it is standard RE stuff, but I found it to be engaging enough to give me incentive to move forward. All in all, another amazing game from amazing company that keeps getting better and better somehow.

Resident Evil Requiem is one of the best survival horror action experiences you could ever have or hope for. This is the 9th main line entry into Capcom’s long running series and you play as two characters this time. The new debut character you play as is Grace Ashcroft. Her game play sections are largely reminiscent of the classic survival horror gameplay from RE 7 and the original fixed camera games of REs 1-3. You will be solving puzzles, managing limited resources with minimal inventory space, engaging in light combat, and sometimes using stealth to evade a pursuing enemy. The man, the legend, and everyone’s favorite Resident Evil character, Leon S Kennedy is back in this entry as well. His gameplay is of course very action combat focused much like RE 4, 5, and 6. He has a multitude of guns and weapons to play around with as well as the ability to initiate stylish combat finishers on enemies. When you’re playing as Leon it feels great and you’re usually the scariest thing in the room. His gameplay sections are nice breaks in between Grace’s scarier and sometimes more stressful gameplay.  Grace’s sections also feel great too. Her levels feel really well designed and are genuinely terrifying on a first play-through. You can also change the perspective of each character from either 1st or 3rd person if you desire. My first playthrough I played Grace’s parts in first person and Leon’s in 3rd as the developers intended. I highly recommend playing this way your first time through. Grace’s sections are way scarier in first person and you’re going to want to see how Leon dispatches zombies in 3rd. Capcom’s RE (Reach For the Moon) engine is also doing some crazy black magic in this game much like there previous RE games. This is graphically one of the best looking games to date. The lighting and visuals look absolutely incredible and really add to the atmosphere. Characters and texture work look incredibly realistic. Requiem is also very well optimized. I played this game with a RTX 5080 and didn’t experience any major technical issues. Make sure you have beefier hardware if you’re planning on playing this with Path tracing and or max settings. I also really enjoyed the story told in this game. Story isn’t always the strongest aspect in RE games but this one had a great balance of tone between thematically dark subject matter and heart warming character dynamics between the cast. Grace Ashcroft is now one of my favorite characters. Her character goes through some brutal moments throughout the game but I enjoyed seeing her development and how she survives the numerous challenges placed in front of her. Leon is much older in this game and also facing a series of challenges before him in this game’s narrative. As a long time RE fan, I really enjoyed seeing how his hardened character tackles these new obstacles. He is my favorite RE character so getting to see him and play as him again in a new mainline entry after such a long time was everything I wanted and more. My boy is not only rocking the cheesey one liners but the Hamilton watch and Porche as well. Re Requiem gets its name from being a new game that takes a lot of familiar concepts and callbacks from previous games. It’s very much a weirdly self aware game so I find that you will get way more fulfillment out of the game after playing some of the previous entries in the franchise. At the very least, I recommend playing RE 2 remake and RE 4 remake before jumping into this entry if you’re uninitiated with the franchise. This game is also pretty scary. I still think RE 7 is scarier but this story had some pretty terrifying moments. If you’re not into horror games, I don’t recommend this. I beat this game in two days at about 17 hours on my first play-through. Its that good. I really enjoyed this one a lot. I think overall it’s a fantastic entry that’s definitely in my top 5 RE games. I’m currently on my second play-through and still really enjoying it. Like many other RE games, this one also has a ton of great replay value. If I had to give Requiem some fair criticism, I’d say either characters gameplay sections can feel longer or shorter than the others. I found Leon’s sections in the beginning to be very short compared to some of Grace’s. I found myself wanting more of both after finishing the game though so I guess that’s a testament to how fun this game really is to play. Depending on who you are, you may find the game too short overall, too short in some characters sections, or even exhausting in others. This entry doesn’t separate the characters gameplay sections into two separate campaigns like it does in RE 1 and 2. You will be switching between the two main characters quite often throughout out the run time so you may feel that there is a lack of real long term progression. However, if you are a fan of survival horror or a fan of Resident Evil, you absolutely need to play this game.

Resident Evil Requiem is incredible. The series slowly became one of my favorites ever since I first played Resident Evil 4 when I was 10 years old, and this entry might honestly be one of the most memorable ones yet. For me, it easily lands in the top 5 of the entire series.  Grace’s sections lean heavily into the classic survival horror feel of the early games, while Leon’s sections are pure action in the spirit of Resident Evil 4. The contrast between the two styles keeps the pacing fresh and makes the whole experience feel very dynamic.  The story plays a lot with suspense. Grace leaves you constantly wondering why she’s involved in everything that’s happening, while Leon is dealing with the virus itself and trying to find a cure, all while the game builds this constant tension that time might be running out. Another great aspect is the nostalgia. You see a lot of it during the Raccoon City sections, with small details scattered everywhere, especially inside the police station.  Visually, the game runs on one of the best graphics engines in the industry right now. With path tracing enabled it looks absolutely incredible, and the optimization is something other studios should seriously learn from. The game runs extremely smoothly and I didn’t notice any frame drops even during some pretty intense action moments.  Post-game content is a little light (at least at launch since Mercenaries isn’t included yet), but between the extras and going for all the achievements there’s still plenty of fun to be had if you want to fully complete it.  Overall I loved the experience, although there are still some story details that weren’t fully resolved. Hopefully those will be expanded on in future DLC.

The survival horror is so effective that I was constantly running to the bathroom before leaving the safe rooms so as to not ♥♥♥♥ myself out of fear. You are strapped for resources and have incredibly weak weapons, heavily encouraging you to sneak around or run from enemies instead of dealing with them head-on. Also the voice actors for Grace and the main antagonist absolutely nailed it for their respective parts. I still hear Victor Gideon's creepy-ass monologues in my nightmares.  The Leon sections are enhanced RE4 gameplay and RE6 as it should have been. It is an incredibly well-done power trip with that classic Resident Evil campiness and Leon dropping quippy one-liners in the face of death. This serves as such a relief after you've had your ass cheeks clenched for hours straight playing as Grace. The weapons are weighty and feel satisfying to use, the animations are smooth and over the top in a good way, and you really feel just like a seasoned veteran mowing through zombies like its your weekly yard care.
